articles.title: Criolo celebra 15 anos do álbum 'Nó na orelha' com turnê que se estenderá por 2027, abarcando sete capitais do Brasil | G1
articles.body:
Criolo celebra com show pelo Brasil os 15 anos do álbum que deu projeção nacional ao rapper paulistano em 2011 — Foto: Reprodução

♬ Lançado em abril de 2011, o segundo álbum de Criolo , “Nó na orelha” completa 15 anos em 2026 – efeméride que gera turnê comemorativa da data e do disco que deu projeção nacional ao rapper paulistano, até então conhecido somente no segmento do hip hop.

No domingo, 13 de setembro, Criolo estreou no festival Coala o show “Nó na Orelha – Quinze anos”, orquestrado sob direção artística de Daniel Ganjaman e Marcelo Cabral, produtores musicais do álbum que extrapolou o universo do rap com gêneros musicais como samba, bolero e reggae, rendendo sucessos como “Bogotá”, “Freguês da meia-noite”, “Não existe amor em SP” – a grande composição do álbum, já abordada por artistas como Célia (1947 – 2017), Emicida (em álbum ao vivo com Criolo), Milton Nascimento (com Criolo) e Paulo Miklos – e “Subirusdoistiozin”.

Na sequência não imediata, Criolo apresentará o show em Salvador (BA) em 8 de novembro, dentro da programação do festival AfroPunk. Um mês depois, em 13 de dezembro, o cantor e compositor faz o show no festival Psica, em Belém (PA). Mas não ficará nisso.

A turnê “Nó na Orelha – Quinze anos” se estenderá por 2027, abarcando ao todo sete capitais do Brasil entre abril e maio. A primeira apresentação de 2027 está programada para 4 de abril, na Fundição Progresso, na cidade do Rio de Janeiro (RJ).

Na sequência da retomada da turnê no Rio de Janeiro (RJ), o artista apresentará o show “Nó na Orelha – Quinze anos” em Belo Horizonte (MG) na Arena Hall, em 10 de abril; em Curitiba (PR) no Cine Lido, em 23 de abril; em Porto Alegre (RS) no Auditório Araújo Vianna, em 24 de abril; e novamente em São Paulo (SP) no Suhai Music Hall, em 8 de maio.

articles.title: Jovem de 16 anos morre antes de show do Stray Kids na Argentina | G1
articles.standfirst: Adolescente sofreu parada cardiorrespiratória na fila no Hipódromo de San Isidro. Grupo de K-pop que esteve no Brasil durante o Rock in Rio prestou homenagem.
articles.summary: Adolescente sofreu parada cardiorrespiratória na fila no Hipódromo de San Isidro. Grupo de K-pop que esteve no Brasil durante o Rock in Rio prestou homenagem.
articles.body:
Stray Kids no palco Mundo do Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Leo Franco/AgNews

Uma jovem de 16 anos morreu nesta segunda-feira (14) pouco antes de entrar no show do grupo de K-pop Stray Kids, na Argentina.

Antes de se apresentar no país, o octeto passou pelo Brasil como atração principal no Palco Mundo do Rock in Rio na última sexta-feira (11).

Segundo o jornal argentino "La Nación", a adolescente desmaiou na fila antes de acessar o Hipódromo de San Isidro, região de Buenos Aires.

Ela foi socorrida e levada a um hospital próximo, mas não resistiu. As autoridades locais informaram que a causa da morte foi uma parada cardiorrespiratória.

O grupo sul-coreano tem dois shows marcados na Argentina, com a segunda apresentação realizada nesta terça-feira (15).

Antes de subir ao palco, a produção do evento divulgou um comunicado em espanhol e inglês lamentando a tragédia e pediu um minuto de silêncio em memória da adolescente.

"Lamentamos profundamente esta perda e queremos expressar nossas mais sinceras condolências e pêsames à família, amigos e entes queridos nesse momento tão difícil."

articles.title: Ed Sheeran: artistas deixam turnê após expulsão de Macklemore | G1
articles.standfirst: Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham e a banda Beoga declararam decisão um dia depois da expulsão de Macklemore. Todos também reforçaram apoio à Palestina.
articles.summary: Finneas e outros músicos cancelam participação na turnê de Ed Sheeran em solidariedade a Macklemore e apoio à Palestina, afetando inclusive os shows marcados no Brasil.
articles.body:
Ed Sheeran se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Gustavo Wanderley/g1

Os cantores Finneas, Aaron Rowe e Lukas Graham e a banda Beoga declararam nesta terça-feira (15) que não vão mais abrir shows de Ed Sheeran, um dia após o anúncio de que Macklemore seria retirado da turnê por causa de seu discurso pró-Palestina .

Com isso, Sheeran agora perdeu todos os os artistas de abertura de sua turnê, que tem datas previstas até o dia 11 de dezembro.

Finneas, aliás, abriria os eventos do cantor britânico em São Paulo nos dias 5 e 6 de dezembro. A banda Beoga, além de abrir shows, também tocava com Sheeran em trechos das apresentações influenciadas pela música irlandesa.

Junto de suas decisões, os três cantores e o grupo declararam apoio ao povo palestino.

"Artistas não devem ser silenciados por se manifestar contra a opressão", escreveu Finneas, em seu Instagram.

"Deveríamos poder falar sobre guerra, sobre civis sendo mortos, sobre crianças que merecem crescer. Onde quer que vivam. Qualquer seja sua bandeira", afirmou Graham.

"Como irlandeses, conhecemos bem até demais genocídio, fome forçada e ocupação violenta", disse Rowe.

"Somos irlandeses que entendem colonialismo. Como membros fundadores do movimento Artistas Irlandeses pela Palestina, somos ativistas com compromisso pela justiça e continuaremos a ser", publicou a Beoga.

Sheeran ainda não comentou a saída dos amigos da turnê.

Expulsão de Macklemore e defesa de Sheeran

Macklemore foi expulso da turnê nesta segunda-feira (14), após pressão de diversos locais onde aconteceriam apresentações de Sheeran pelos Estados Unidos.

Segundo o jornal "The Guardian", em um breve discurso entre as músicas, no dia 4 de setembro, o artista disse "Free Palestine" (Palestina Livre) no palco e afirmou que queria que pessoas em Gaza e na Cisjordânia soubessem que não haviam sido esquecidas. A declaração motivou uma petição do Conselho Israelense-Americano (Israeli American Council) pedindo sua retirada da turnê.

O rapper divulgou um comunicado sobre sua saída. "Antes de começar, quero dizer algo que deveria ser óbvio. Neste momento, acho que isso importa. Eu não sou uma vítima”, escreveu Macklemore no Instagram. "As vítimas são o povo palestino."

O cantor britânico afirmou que a decisão partiu da promotora da turnê, a Messina Touring Group. "Não sou cúmplice. Tenho minhas visões pessoais sobre esse conflito devastador. Só porque eu escolho não falar publicamente, não significa que eu não as tenho, e não significa que eu não ligo", publicou Sheeran.

Um comitê de investigação contratado pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) apontou em junho que Israel alvejou crianças deliberadamente na Faixa de Gaza . Segundo a comissão, tais práticas em Gaza configuram genocídio, crimes contra a humanidade e crimes de guerra.

O relatório da comissão da ONU afirmou ainda que cerca de 30% dos 73 mil mortos na guerra em Gaza eram crianças, pouco mais de 20 mil em números absolutos.

articles.title: DJ e produtor mineiro Bronka conecta o funk brasileiro ao universo 'clubber' da Alemanha no EP 'EDM de quebrada' | G1
articles.body:
Capa do EP 'EDM de quebrada', do DJ e produtor musical mineiro Bronka — Foto: Marian E. Studio / Divulgação

♬ Nascido em Montes Claros (MG) e radicado em Frankfurt, na Alemanha, o DJ e produtor musical mineiro Bronka dá sequência ao processo de inserção do funk brasileiro no universo da música eletrônica alemã com o EP “EDM de quebrada” – no mundo a partir de amanhã, quarta-feira, 16 de setembro, com cinco faixas e capa que expõe o artista em foto de Marian E. Studio.

Nome em ascensão nas pistas europeias e asiáticas, Bronka parte do funk brasileiro e da bass music nacional para conectar essas referências com acid, breakbeat , dubstep e techno dentro de estética clubber evocativa das raves dos anos 1990 e 2000.

Precedido pelo single que apresentou em 6 de agosto a faixa “Vem PPK”, o EP “EDM de quebrada” é o resultado de onze anos de vivência do DJ na cena eletrônica alemã, na qual debutou em 2015. É nessa ponte Brasil-Alemanha que transita o EP “EDM de quebrada” com escalas no Irã, na Indonésia e nos Estados Unidos.

Parceria de Bronka com o produtor iraniano Q-Rush, gravada com participação do MC nova-iorquino Stimulus, “Break iraniano” abre o EP com mix de breakbeat , beat bolha e referências da música popular do Irã, incluindo samples de dois temas desse país.

Em “Bonde do Vandal”, Bronka se junta ao produtor holandês-surinamês Jarreau Vandal em combinação de funk sobre base de dubstep. Já “Se concentra” é faixa produzida por Bronka com o DJ e produtor paulista DJ Saze. O tema parte da house para transitar por breakbeat com vocais de MC Buret e MC BF.

Fechando o EP, “Vem de 4” é produzida por Bronka om o indonésio Naken, nome que reitera a diversidade intercontinental dos colaboradores do DJ mineiro no EP “EDM de quebrada”.

articles.title: 'Widow's Bay' won big, Mariska nailed it and Taylor Swift spoofed 'SVU': The 2026 Emmys, from every angle
articles.summary: From Mariska Hargitay's many outfit changes to Zendaya and Tom Holland's charm offensive, the Emmys delivered all around.
articles.body:
What a night, eh? Emmys host Mariska Hargitay presided over an evening of laughs, tears (Noah Kahan singing "Bridge Over Troubled Water" during the In Memoriam? Pass the tissues.) and Taylor Swift. To break down TV's biggest night, we enlisted our best experts — from our resident TV critic to style pros to internet culture vultures to boots-on-the-ground correspondents reporting live from the red carpet and press room.

Here's what they'll remember most from the 2026 Emmys — good and bad.

Cutest couple goes to Zendaya and Tom Holland

There's something refreshing about an A-list, box-office star who has absolutely no problem being the plus-one. Of course, when your plus-one is your wife, Zendaya, it's a pretty great gig. Tom Holland came to the Emmys on Monday night simply to support Zendaya, who was nominated for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series for the third and final season of Euphoria .

While she walked the red carpet solo, Holland quietly slipped inside — but once the show started, the famously low-key couple wasn't exactly hard to spot. Holland enthusiastically cheered Zendaya on when her category was announced, even though the award ultimately went to Rhea Seehorn. And throughout the night, the two seemed perfectly content, making the Emmys their own very glamorous date night.

They caught up with friends, including Ayo Edebiri, and shared a particularly sweet moment with Mark Ruffalo, laughing together before Zendaya and Holland each pulled him in for a hug. For two of the biggest movie stars in the world, they somehow still give off the energy of a couple who are just genuinely happy to be hanging out together. No grand red carpet couple moment required.

Taryn Ryder , senior entertainment reporter

Matthew Rhys was definitely the most popular celeb of the night. Are we even surprised, though? He took home two awards and was a total crowd-pleaser in the press room, where I was stationed for the night. He readily gushed over Widow's Bay executive producer and director Hiro Murai when I asked him about balancing horror and comedy and quipped about having a playful rivalry with his partner, The Diplomat star Keri Russell, who was also nominated tonight. When he was told his time was up, he genuinely seemed bummed out. He loved chatting with us, and we loved chatting with him!

Neia Balao , entertainment and lifestyle reporter

This awards season is picking up where last year's left off: Feathers are still very much the moment. They were everywhere, from neckline trims, like the pink layers on Allison Janney's black gown and the feather effect on Nicole Kidman's snowy Chanel dress, to full-length fringe, like Jaclyn Smith's seafoam number. It's a trend I'm already adding to my own cart, if I'm being honest.

Nineties fashion isn't the only thing making a comeback — the decade's hair is having its own little reunion tour, and nowhere was that clearer than during tonight's ceremony. Rachel Sennott was among a handful of attendees who went sky-high with their ponytails in a way that was pure '90s slumber party-energy. Meanwhile, Florence Pugh showed up in a spiky, piecey updo that was bold, delightfully unhinged and gave me slight prom-war flashbacks. (A cosmic force may have added some styling paste to my cart right now.) Now, the style isn't something that would work on just anybody, but Pugh obviously pulls it off.

Elsewhere on the red carpet, the throwbacks kept coming, just less obviously '90s. There were some teasing, some slicked-back buns and sleek middle parts, though Shailene Woodley's low, center ponytail had more of a 1970s cult energy. (Is there a Manson family film somewhere on the horizon that I don't know about?) However, it still tracks since the actual '90s were never just about one overarching look. The decade swung from grunge to glam to minimalism to maximalism, so it makes sense that tonight didn't settle on a single '90s archetype either.

The Emmys carpet may be blue, but this year's looks were red-hot. Host Mariska Hargitay stunned in floor-length sequins in a screaming five-alarm red that would probably make Jessica Rabbit do a double-take. Plenty more stunned in similarly bold tones, including Niecy Nash-Betts, Brooks Nader, Jessica Belkin, Cailee Spaeny, Rhea Seehorn and Jackie Tohn, while even more embraced a rich burgundy, including Taylor Dearden, Fiona Dourif, Calista Flockhart and Cynthia Nixon, who was deemed "best dressed" by E!'s Keltie Knight early in the night for her asymmetrical textured Issey Miyake gown. The good news: You don't have to spend a bundle to channel her look.

There's been some talk on the internet lately about whether red lips are "outdated" — an argument I don't think holds up when red lips have been a look for literal centuries. The Emmys proved that a crimson mouth goes beyond any trend cycle. Cailee Spaeny and Jackie Tohn were refreshingly unafraid to go full makeup-monotone, matching their red lips to their gowns, while Dakota Fanning and Emmy Rossum used theirs as a pop of color instead. One thing that's always worked in red lipstick's favor? There are plenty of drugstore formulas that perform just as well as the high-end ones. (I should know, I have all of them!)

For those who prefer something more understated, nudes were the other lip look all over the ceremony. Odessa A'zion, Zendaya and Kristen Bell were among the stars who went the subtle route. It's also just as easy — a defined lip liner and a swipe of gloss can get you that same look without committing to a full matte neutral.

I'll never not love an outfit that's basically encrusted in gems , so it's no surprise that my favorite looks of the night were the big swings that landed, especially the sculptural gowns with 3D effects that toed the line between architecture and fashion. My top picks: Selena Gomez's Louis Vuitton dress that looked like it was constructed with stacks of gold bricks, Zendaya's custom Prada gown that literally dripped in gems and Chase Infiniti's Louis Vuitton mermaid gown that evoked a web of copper bubbles woven together. BTW, Linda Cardellini has never looked better than she does tonight in a mother-of-pearl tiled gown by Yara Shoemaker.

My favorite look of the night goes to Elle Fanning, who was nominated for Margo's Got Money Trouble s. She wore a strappy, jade-green Ralph Lauren gown with a dramatic train and delicate tassel detailing, with a muted red lip and her blond hair in loose curls. Is the energy fairy or mermaid? Either way, I love it. That sort of mint-jade green is an unexpected and underrated red carpet color that always gets my attention. And the fact that she paired it with platforms in the same jade shade instead of gold or silver is a real power move. Brava!

Well, that was a long night for Mariska Hargitay, who seemed to live an entirely new life with every costume change during her duties as Emmys host. When she arrived on the red carpet in a Jessica Rabbit-inspired red sequin gown, I thought that she couldn't possibly look any better. And then she did — in the silver strapless gown she wore to take the stage for her opening monologue. And again in black satin with gold embellishments. And then came pink sequins, followed by a black strapless gown with leather gloves.

There was her Game of Thrones look, which she was admittedly sweating through, before she changed into — what else? — another stunning sequin dress. If you're having trouble keeping up, that brings us to seven looks. There were still four more to come. Making the whole thing even more confusing — and impressive — were the drastic hair transformations between outfits. Over the course of the three-hour show, Hargitay went from mid-length beachy waves to cascading Old Hollywood curls and, ultimately, a chin-length bob. Naturally, she pulled off every version flawlessly and made the whole production look effortless. Now I'm left with two questions: What exactly was happening backstage to make all that glam possible? And has anyone checked on her styling team?

Kerry Justich , senior lifestyle reporter

Mariska Hargitay makes the case for a comedic role

Though we know and love her as the stern cop with a heart of gold, Olivia Benson, Mariska Hargitay showed that she has comedic chops too. She had me rolling on the floor with her jokes about Dick Wolf and the number of Emmys she's won for Law and Order: Special Victims Unit. Zero is a number!

My personal favorite joke came during her monologue, when she referenced Nicole Kidman's iconic AMC Theaters ad — and when Kidman responded, Hargitay ordered her to "zip it, movie lady."

I also have to give a shoutout to Jalen Brunson's appearance in Hargitay's opening number. He'll also be making his comedic debut soon, when he hosts Saturday Night Live later this month.

Kelsey Weekman , senior entertainment reporter

There were predictable yet deserving wins like The Pitt , Jean Smart and Stephen Colbert, but there were also more unexpected wins than usual: Sally Field for the straight-to-streaming Netflix film Remarkably Bright Creatures, Allison Janney for The Diplomat , Tom Pelphrey for Task and Slow Horses in directing, to name a few. It's possible that vote splitting contributed to some of these surprises, especially given the many nominations for The Pitt. On this, I say competition is healthy, and an upset is always more exciting than straight-across sweep domination.

Michel Ghanem, Trust Me, I Watch Everything TV critic and writer behind TV Scholar

One such surprise became the highlight of the evening: Apple TV's word-of-mouth horror-comedy hit Widow's Bay . The entertaining series follows the mayor of a small island off the coast of New England as he tries his best to revitalize it for tourism, despite one big problem: it's haunted. Historically, the Emmys have not been kind to horror. Some of the highlights of the genre, like The Haunting of Hill House , were previously completely shut out. The infusion of comedy into Widow's Bay made it stand out as something unique, and it's also possible recent sci-fi shows like Severance helped open the door for Emmy voters to consider more fantastical options (rather than a grounded comedy like Margo's Got Money Troubles ). Widow's Bay is walking away with the most awards of the night.

It's too bad to see a show like Love Story walk away empty-handed ( DTF St. Louis was pretty much a guaranteed win after Linda Cardellini and David Harbour snagged wins last weekend at the Creative Arts ceremony for their supporting roles).

Finally, when we step back and look at the overall winning slate, a worrying pattern emerges: Not a single actor of color was awarded tonight. Hollywood, especially after 2020, made a concerted push to commission more stories at the margins and cast in a representative way. This year's wins feel like the official end of that era, in a way. Each of tonight's winners is talented — but it's a concerning trend of the kinds of shows being greenlit and highlighted more broadly, and something I'll be keeping an eye on as a critic.

Meg Stalter delivers the standout red carpet look — again

Never one to miss a chance to reference something funny on the red carpet, nominee Meg Stalter stole the pre-show by dressing up in gold and body paint to resemble an Emmy statuette.

She committed to the bit, wearing the body paint to the ceremony as well, where she cheered on costar Jean Smart as she won the award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series. I have to wonder if the chair she's been sitting in all night has turned gold too.

In the past, Stalter has dressed as Kylie Jenner (to Paul W. Downs's Timothée Chalamet), a coffee cup and Diet Coke . I loved it when she wore a basic white tee and jeans to last year's Emmys.

Taylor Swift makes a surprise appearance (and drops some Easter eggs)

I have to apologize to everyone I scoffed at when they asked if Taylor Swift would be at the Emmys because technically she was, even though she was physically at her husband's football game, hanging out with Tom Cruise.

Swift made an appearance in a pre-taped sketch, in which she plays a detective helping the cast of Law and Order: Special Victims Unit try to figure out … well, whether Taylor Swift was coming to the Emmys. Classic conundrum.

I should have known she'd do a favor for her pal Mariska Hargitay — one of Swift's cats is named after Hargitay's iconic character, Olivia Benson, and that's a bond far stronger than marriage.

Since she can only ever be herself, Swift joked about her penchant for Easter eggs and her fans' passion for decoding them — while dropping a few herself. Does anyone know what " saccharide, Aeries, from the vineyard, north or south " means?

articles.title: 'People who rejected me are calling now': 'Hanuman Ansh' composer on life after film's succes
articles.summary: Hanuman Ansh, made on a modest budget of Rs 2 crore, has emerged as one of the biggest surprise hits at the box office this year. Despite opening to a.
articles.body: Hanuman Ansh, made on a modest budget of Rs 2 crore, has emerged as one of the biggest surprise hits at the box office this year. Despite opening to a mere Rs 10 lakh, the film has gone on to earn crores daily and has now crossed the Rs 200 crore mark in India. Alongside its box office run, the film's music has also taken over social media, with countless reels and videos built around its songs.In conversation with Hindustan Times, music composer Dhirendra Mulkalwar spoke about how opportunities are now coming from the same industry that once turned him away.Composer calls the success a miracleReflecting on 'Hanuman Ansh's massive Rs 200 crore collection, music composer Dhirendra Mulkalwar admitted that the team is still coming to terms with it. He said, "This is like a miracle for us. We still don't know how to react to it. I think we have surrendered ourselves and are seeing it as a blessing from Babji, actually."Life after the film's successWith 'Hanuman Ansh' now a certified hit, Dhirendra shared how his professional life has transformed almost overnight. He said, "Phone calls are coming in with people congratulating me. I am getting some offers and am in talks for some of them. I am very hopeful. Before Hanuman Ansh, I was unsure whether I would be able to make a career in films, but Baba Ji has given me such a big success. Now I have left it all to him. I am getting calls from people who had rejected me before. So, I am very positive and hopeful."Role of social media in the film's riseSpeaking about how the film gained momentum despite a shrinking number of screens, Dhirendra credited social media and grassroots promotion. He said, "In the second week, when our screens were reduced to just 30, Vishal and the entire team travelled from city to city in their cars, from Mumbai to Surat and then to Delhi, to promote the film."He added, "On social media, people could see that those coming out after watching the film had tears in their eyes. So, all of this happened organically. Social media played a very big role in the upward trend we saw in the box office collections and the number of screens increasing."More about 'Hanuman Ansh'Directed by Vishal Chaturvedi and starring Shobhinaw Satyaa as Neem Karoli Baba, the film was released on August 7, 2026.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Biggest OTT platform rejected 'Hanuman Ansh,' says director as he opens up on his 14 year struggle to make the Rs 200 crore grosser: 'Steve Jobs visited Neem Karoli Baba's ashram'
articles.summary: Director Vishal Chaturvedi’s ‘Hanuman Ansh’, based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, has turned into one of the biggest box-office surprises of 2026. T.
articles.body: Director Vishal Chaturvedi’s ‘Hanuman Ansh’, based on the life of Neem Karoli Baba, has turned into one of the biggest box-office surprises of 2026. The film, which opened to a mere Rs 10 lakh in India and struggled to find an audience during its first two weeks, has witnessed a remarkable turnaround and is now recording strong collections even on weekdays.According to industry tracker Sacnilk, ‘Hanuman Ansh’ has collected Rs 222.88 crore nett in India, while its worldwide gross stands at Rs 277.80 crore. The film is currently the third-highest-grossing Indian release of 2026, behind ‘Dhurandhar: The Revenge’ (Rs 1,813.39 crore) and ‘Border 2’ (Rs 450.19 crore). Made on a reported budget of less than Rs 2 crore, the film has also emerged as one of the most profitable releases of the decade, with its returns estimated at nearly 140 times its production cost.As the devotional drama continues its impressive theatrical run, an interview with doctor-turned-filmmaker Vishal Chaturvedi has been gaining attention online. In his conversation with The Indian Thing, the filmmaker opened up about the long and difficult journey behind ‘Hanuman Ansh’, including the setbacks he faced while trying to get his projects off the ground.“It took 14 years after leaving the medical profession for me to make Hanuman Ansh,” he revealed during a conversation with The Indian Thing. “I wanted to make my first film in the second or third year after leaving the medical profession, but couldn’t. It’s not like anyone who steps into the industry will become a director. I began working on the film during the COVID era.”He recalled how the pandemic deeply affected him, particularly after losing several people close to him. “A lot of people close to me, including my best friend’s mother, my first cousin, and my mentor, died during that period in a span of five to six days. It affected me mentally, as I couldn’t help anyone despite being a doctor. During the second wave of COVID, I began feeling an urge to do something positive. So, I started a group called Hanuman Chalisa on Clubhouse. The intent was simple: share your woes, or if you want to pray for your family, you can by reciting Hanuman Chalisa. People from different parts of the world joined it eventually.”At the same time, Chaturvedi was trying to find his footing in the film industry, but several projects failed to materialise. “A big film of mine had been announced, but it wasn’t going on floors. In between, I signed two or three more things. There was a Hotstar show as well, which was launched, but then it was called off. These were becoming too taxing,” he shared.His fascination with Lord Hanuman and Neem Karoli Baba, however, had been around for much longer. “I was always fascinated by Hanuman ji as a character. The idea came to my mind about 20 years ago. I had been travelling with it since then, narrating Neem Karoli Baba’s story to everyone. Once I began telling them I was going to make a film on him, their main question was, ‘Who would play Baba?'” he added.Getting the film made proved to be another challenge, with even a major OTT platform turning down the concept. Chaturvedi recalled pitching ideas to what he described as the biggest OTT platform in the world.“Once, I approached the biggest OTT platform in the world to pitch concepts. As they liked my first two, they asked if I had Indian concepts with international relevance. Excited, I told them about Neem Karoli Baba. I said, ‘It is the story from India for the world,’ because tech giants Apple, Meta and Google had some stories related to him.”He then explained why he believed Baba’s story had global relevance. “Steve Jobs visited India 13 days after Baba’s death, stayed at his ashram, and probably drew inspiration for Apple from there, rooted in minimalism. Then, Steve Jobs asked Mark Zuckerberg to visit Baba’s ashram, and he eventually did. I told the two female executives of the OTT platform all this. One of them was from Uttarakhand and was slightly interested in what I was saying, but she was junior to the other. As soon as I finished pitching, the senior bluntly said, ‘We are not looking for such kinds of concepts.’ Their reaction triggered me,” he added.Despite the repeated setbacks, Chaturvedi eventually brought his long-gestating project to the big screen. articles.body: El thriller político que ha cautivado a millones de espectadores está listo para su esperado regreso a la pequeña pantalla. Netflix ha confirmado oficialmente que la cuarta temporada de 'La diplomática' (The Diplomat) llegará a su catálogo global el próximo 15 de octubre. La aclamada ficción regresa para resolver los intensos interrogantes que dejó abiertos en su anterior entrega, prometiendo mantener el ritmo frenético y el ingenio narrativo que la han convertido en uno de los dramas más sólidos de la plataforma. Para quienes aún no se hayan adentrado en su trama, la serie sigue los pasos de Kate Wyler (interpretada por Keri Russell), una diplomática de carrera acostumbrada a gestionar crisis en zonas de conflicto geopolítico. De manera inesperada, en medio de una emergencia internacional, Wyler es nombrada embajadora de Estados Unidos en el Reino Unido. Su labor no solo consiste en frenar guerras a escala mundial, sino también en tejer alianzas estratégicas mientras intenta capear el temporal de un matrimonio convulso con Hal Wyler (Rufus Sewell), un legendario y manipulador diplomático. Acompañando la fecha de lanzamiento, la plataforma ha publicado el tráiler oficial de esta cuarta entrega, desatando la conversación en redes sociales. Las imágenes muestran a una Kate Wyler contra las cuerdas, obligada a tomar decisiones extremas en el corazón de Londres. El adelanto anticipa una escalada en las teorías de conspiración dentro del propio gobierno estadounidense, donde las lealtades personales chocan de frente con la seguridad nacional y las ambiciones del poder con un mensaje claro: "Un arma nuclear robada. Un matrimonio roto. Un presidente impredecible." La nueva temporada mantendrá el formato habitual de la producción y constará de 8 capítulos, los cuales se estrenarán de forma simultánea el día señalado para permitir a los fans disfrutar del maratón completo. La dirección mantiene el tono ágil, combinando diálogos mordaces sobre la alta política internacional con el dramatismo cotidiano de sus personajes principales. Con esta cuarta tanda de episodios, 'La diplomática' busca consolidarse definitivamente en la cúspide del género de suspense político. articles.title: Quote of the day by Michael Douglas: ‘My dad was a movie star. Having that name was good and bad. People think it’s a silver spoon. It’s not,' a personal anecdote from the star on growing up in Kirk Douglas’ shadow and a powerful life lesson about carving your own path
articles.summary: Michael Douglas shares insights on growing up under the shadow of his father, Kirk Douglas, discussing the duality of having a famous surname and the pressure it brings. Discover his journey of establishing his own career and identity in Hollywood.
articles.body: A famous surname can get people talking before you have even had the chance to introduce yourself. For Michael Douglas, that was part of growing up as the son of Hollywood legend Kirk Douglas. His father was already a major movie star, which meant Michael was familiar with the world of cinema from an early age. It also meant that his own ambitions could easily be viewed through the lens of his father’s success.Michael eventually chose acting, just as his father had done, but his journey was not simply a matter of stepping into an established Hollywood career. He had to find his own place in the industry while dealing with assumptions about the advantages that came with his family nameToday’s quote of the day by Michael Douglas reads: “My dad was a movie star. Having that name was good and bad. People think it’s a silver spoon. It’s not.”What does the quote by Michael Douglas mean?Douglas remarked this while discussing his relationship with his father, Kirk Douglas, in an interview. Fox News reported the interview on August 31, 2018.The phrase “silver spoon” refers to the idea that someone born into a wealthy or influential family automatically receives an easy path in life. Michael Douglas's comment challenges that assumption. Having a famous father certainly brought him closer to Hollywood, but it did not mean that every part of his career was handed to him. There was also the pressure of comparison. As an actor, Kirk Douglas had built a strong reputation, so Michael had to establish himself without being seen only as his son.The quote is interesting because Douglas does not pretend that having a famous father was either completely easy or completely difficult. His family name came with certain advantages, but it also meant that people had their own ideas about how much he had been handed. He still had to prove himself and make a name that was his own.How is the quote by Michael Douglas relevant today?The pressure to live up to a successful parent is not unique to Hollywood. Children of actors, athletes, business leaders and other public figures can find themselves compared with their parents before they have had the opportunity to establish their own identity.Michael’s experience shows why opportunity and pressure can sometimes arrive together. Having access to useful connections or a familiar name can be an advantage, but it does not guarantee that a person will succeed in the long run.His words may also resonate with people who feel they are constantly being measured against someone else. A parent’s achievements can be impressive, but they do not have to become a child’s definition of success. Building a different career, developing a separate reputation or choosing another direction can be just as meaningful.Early life of Michael DouglasMichael Douglas was born on September 25, 1944, in New Brunswick, New Jersey. His parents were actor Kirk Douglas and actress Diana Dill. Growing up, Michael was surrounded by the entertainment industry, although he did not immediately follow his father into acting.He studied drama at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and began his professional career with television work. His early experiences gave him an opportunity to develop away from the enormous reputation his father had already created.Rather than relying entirely on his family connection, Michael gradually built his own experience in front of and behind the camera.Michael Douglas’ rise to fameDouglas became widely recognised through television when he played Steve Keller in ‘The Streets of San Francisco’. The series ran from 1972 to 1977 and gave him a strong platform as a young actor.He also moved into producing, taking on an important role behind the scenes on ‘One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest’. The film won the Academy Award for Best Picture in 1976, giving Douglas an early major achievement outside his father’s shadow.His acting career grew further with films such as ‘The China Syndrome’, ‘Romancing the Stone’ and ‘Fatal Attraction’. ‘Wall Street’ gave Michael Douglas one of the roles that audiences would remember him for. Playing the ambitious Gordon Gekko in Oliver Stone’s 1987 film brought him the Academy Award for Best Actor the following year and added another major achievement to his growing career.Over the years, Douglas built a long-running career in both movies and television, moving comfortably between different kinds of roles. With time, his work established him as a star in his own right rather than simply being known as Kirk Douglas’ son.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Asaltan a mano armada al ciclista Óscar Sevilla en Bogotá: "Salí a entrenar y me encañonaron"
articles.standfirst: Fue víctima de robo a mano armada por dos delincuentes en motocicleta
articles.summary: Fue víctima de robo a mano armada por dos delincuentes en motocicleta
articles.body: El ciclismo colombiano vuelve a ser epicentro de indignación por cuenta de la delincuencia. En la mañana de este martes, el reconocido ciclista español (nacionalizado colombiano) Óscar Sevilla fue víctima de un atraco a mano armada en Bogotá mientras cumplía con su jornada habitual de entrenamiento. El hecho ocurrió aproximadamente a las 8:20 a. m. a la altura de la Autopista Norte con calle 170, en el norte de la ciudad. Según relató el propio corredor a través de sus redes sociales, dos delincuentes que se movilizaban en una motocicleta de alto cilindraje lo abordaron y lo encañonaron con un arma de fuego para despojarlo de sus pertenencias. "Hoy, 8:20 a. m., salí a entrenar y en la Autopista con calle 170 fui interceptado por una moto de alto cilindraje. Me amenazaron con un arma de fuego. No pudieron robarme la bicicleta, pero sí el celular. Pasó una patrulla, denuncié el hecho y me dijeron que no podían hacer nada", manifestó el experimentado ciclista de 49 años. A pesar del susto y la violencia del ataque, Sevilla resultó ileso físicamente y los asaltantes no lograron llevarse su bicicleta de competencia. Sin embargo, la situación generó fuerte malestar en el deportista debido a la inacción de las autoridades al momento de avisar a una patrulla de la Policía Nacional que transitaba por el sector. Por su parte, su escuadra deportiva, el Team Medellín EPM, emitió un mensaje de apoyo al corredor y rechazó firmemente el acto delictivo: "Dos hombres armados, en una moto, lo intimidaron para quitarle el celular. Por fortuna, Óscar está bien. Desde el Team Medellín EPM rechazamos estos hechos que afectan no solo a Óscar, sino a toda la ciudadanía". El caso de Óscar Sevilla reabre el debate sobre la falta de garantías de seguridad para los ciclistas profesionales y aficionados que transitan a diario por los corredores viales de Bogotá y sus alrededores. No es la primera vez que el corredor sufre un hecho delictivo en la capital. El episodio vuelve a encender las alarmas entre la comunidad deportista, que exige a la Alcaldía Mayor y a la Policía Metropolitana reforzar la vigilancia en los puntos críticos de entrenamiento de la ciudad.

articles.title: Christian Bale opens foster care village to keep siblings together
articles.summary: The "Batman Begins" actor attended the opening of the new facility.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Actor Christian Bale helped create a new foster care village that aims to keep siblings together.

Bale attended the opening of Together California in Palmdale, California, which is described as the first village of its kind in the state.

The goal of the facility will be to keep siblings together while they are in the foster care system, something uncommon for children in foster care .

The community includes 12 furnished homes and is designed to provide a safe environment for children and their families, along with programs focused on stability. There are also gardens and a community center on the 4.7-acre property.

The project is funded through donations, including nearly $9 million raised by the Austrian American Council West.

Bale reportedly invested $22 million of his own into the project, which was 17 years in the making.

The "Batman Begins" star has no history with the foster care system but said he became interested in the issue after having his own children.

Now that the village is open, children are expected to begin moving in next month.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran Fallout: Tour Openers Finneas, Lukas Graham and Aaron Rowe Drop in Solidarity With Macklemore
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran's house band and opener Aaron Rowe have dropped out of tour in solidarity to Macklemore.
articles.body:
Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour is coming apart at the seams as Finneas, opener Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham, and Sheeran's own house band Beoga have all dropped out in solidarity with Macklemore's dismissal – which leaves the remainder of his tour without an opener.

Finneas, who was slated to join Sheeran on the South American portion of the tour, announced he was dropping out on Instagram Tuesday.

"Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed," he wrote. "I have decided to withdraw my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran. I stand with Palestine and its people."

Rowe posted to Instagram on Tuesday as well, notifying his fans of his choice to drop out as Sheeran's opener.

"I have made the decision to withdraw as a support act for Ed Sheeran's 'The Loop' North American Tour," Rowe wrote. "I don't take the decision lightly. Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this."

He added: "But as Irish people, we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation. I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide and who highlight the savage murder of children. I would lose all respect for myself to carry on as normal. I need to be true to myself and my ancestors who resisted colonisation, and fought for a freedom that I enjoy today in Ireland."

Sheeran's house band Beoga also added their names to the list of artists who were leaving the Loop Tour. Graham joined the cavalcade of dropouts shortly after.

"We have been friends with Ed for over 10 years now and will continue to be," the band wrote on their own Instagram . "We believe in dialogue as a means of progressing the plight of the Palestinian people … We are Irish people who understand colonialism. As founding members of the Irish Artists for Palestine movement, we are committed activists for justice and will continue to be."

With all the dropouts, that leaves the Sheeran's remaining tour dates without a single opener. The Loop Tour was in progress when Macklemore was dropped and was planned to run through December. Finneas was scheduled to join for the South American leg of the tour which begins in November.

Representatives for Sheeran did not immediately return TheWrap's request for comment.

Sheeran shared his side of the story earlier on Tuesday, a day after Macklemore was dropped from the Loop Tour for sharing his pro-Palestine stance onstage.

"Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter's decision. It was not mine. Macklemore's contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me," Sheeran explained. "I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living."

The "Shape of You" singer's statement appears to corroborate both Macklemore and Robert Kraft's version of events after the rapper blamed the billionaire for his removal due to his "Free Palestine" messaging.

Macklemore was originally scheduled to open for eight more shows on Sheeran's tour, kicking back up Friday in Philadelphia. These updates come a week after the Israeli American Council condemned his pro-Palestine messaging , issuing a petition for his removal from the tour.

For his part, Macklemore made sure to point out that "Antisemitism is real" in his initial statement, while also noting that "more than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone."

"Ed was in a f–ked up position. He knew it. His typical apolitical stance was being challenged in a way it never had been before," Macklemore wrote on Monday. "But he couldn't get past his public-facing 'I don't take sides.'"

He finished: "I didn't need 10 shows from Ed. I needed two. Two chances to stand in front of 90,000 people and say the words that somehow became too dangerous to say. Free Palestine. If those words cost me the stage, while turning the conversation back to Palestine, then it was the most successful tour I've been on."

articles.title: Amanda Seyfried and Thomas Sadoski Split After 9 Years of Marriage (Exclusive)
articles.summary: “We’ve got each other forever—and it’s GOOD,” the actors, who were married in 2017, said in a joint statement exclusively to PEOPLE
articles.body:
Amanda Seyfried and Thomas Sadoski have split after nine years, the couple confirm exclusively to PEOPLE

The stars, who married in 2017, share two children and have largely kept their family life private

They first met in 2015 while working together and later supported each other's careers and humanitarian efforts

Amanda Seyfried and Thomas Sadoski are going their separate ways after nine years of marriage.

The actors confirmed their split in a joint statement exclusively to PEOPLE, saying they have been separated "for a while" and that the decision has ultimately been the right one for their family.

"We have been separated for a while, and it's proven to be the right move for us and our family unit. We've got each other forever—and it's GOOD," Seyfried and Sadoski said in their statement.

Seyfried, 40, and Sadoski, 50, first met in 2015 while starring together in the off-Broadway play The Way We Get By .

The pair reunited later that year on the set of The Last Word , in which they played love interests. By the following spring, their on-screen connection had become a real-life romance, with PEOPLE confirming they were dating in March 2016 .

"We eloped. We just took off into the country with an officiant and, just the two of us, and we did our thing," Sadoski said at the time. "It was beautiful. It was everything that it should be. It was just the two of us talking to each other."

Just days after their wedding, the couple welcomed their first child, daughter Nina . They later welcomed a son, Thomas Jr. , in September 2020.

Over the years, Seyfried and Sadoski largely kept their family life private, settling into a quieter lifestyle on a farm in upstate New York. Seyfried occasionally offered glimpses of their life together, including their family routine, their animals and their shared work supporting children affected by conflict.

In 2017, shortly after their wedding, Sadoski opened up about Seyfried, saying, "She's the person that I love, admire, respect most in the world."

The couple also continued to support each other professionally and publicly. Seyfried thanked Sadoski during her 2022 Emmy acceptance speech after winning Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie for The Dropout , while Sadoski joined her on the red carpet for the 2023 premiere of The Crowded Room .

In 2023, Seyfried described the pair as " yin and yang " when it came to parenting, while Sadoski spoke about how proud he was to work alongside his wife supporting War Child USA.

In January 2026, Seyfried spoke about Sadoski's support for her career during a particularly busy period, telling Vogue that her husband "sacrifices a lot for me" as she took on roles in The Testament of Ann Lee , The Housemaid and the series Long Bright River .

The actress posted a photo of Sadoski on her Instagram Stories on Sept. 15, showing him posing playfully with a gecko. "@thomassadoski is a #reptiledad," she wrote.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran says he tried to ‘build a bridge’ over Macklemore tour spot before venues said no
articles.summary: Ed Sheeran says Macklemore's removal from his "Loop Tour" was the concert promoter's decision, not his, after U.S. venues threatened to pull shows.
articles.body: Ed Sheeran addressed Macklemore’s removal from his U.S. tour Tuesday, saying the rapper’s departure was ultimately a decision made by the concert promoter and venues — not by him. The "Shape of You" singer said he was "appalled" by the conflict between Israel and Palestine and described the suffering on both sides as "a human tragedy," according to a lengthy statement shared on Instagram after Macklemore accused Sheeran and tour organizers of sidelining him over his pro-Palestinian remarks. Following Sheeran's note, four supporting acts withdrew from the Loop Tour in solidarity with Macklemore, including Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, Lukas Graham, and Finneas. MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE "Macklemore asked to join my tour last year and I agreed, because I respect him as an artist," Sheeran wrote. "As with all my support acts, I agree that they play a setlist of their choosing." On Monday, Macklemore had claimed that Sheeran told him Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, had rallied other stadium owners to oppose allowing the rapper to perform. According to his account, the venues allegedly gave Sheeran an ultimatum: "if Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues." Sheeran’s statement offered a different account of the events, saying that after Macklemore’s performances at his New Jersey shows, venues scheduled for upcoming tour dates told organizers they would pull the shows if Macklemore remained on the lineup. "After Macklemore’s performances at my New Jersey shows, venues on my upcoming tour dates communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting," Sheeran wrote. "I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of his message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said. I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge. One of those people was Robert Kraft. I was also involved in direct talks with promoters along with activists on both sides to try and find a mutual resolution for all, but the venue’s and promoter’s decision was final." MICHAEL RAPAPORT SLAMS 'CLOWN' MACKLEMORE FOR ANTI-ISRAEL PERFORMANCE "Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine," Sheeran added. "Macklemore’s contract for the tour was with the promoter, not me." Macklemore was scheduled to perform at eight of the remaining U.S. dates on Sheeran’s "Loop Tour." Sheeran said he has deliberately avoided using his professional platform for politics because his audience includes young people and children from diverse backgrounds. Sheeran said concertgoers attend his shows expecting "a place of safety and sanctuary" rather than a political forum. "There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics – my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds," he wrote. "Those who come to my shows do not expect a political forum. I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes. However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed. If we only focus on shouting the loudest, nothing will ever change. There are different approaches to being an advocate for change." Sheeran also rejected the suggestion that his decision not to speak publicly about his personal beliefs made him indifferent to the conflict. "I am not complicit," he wrote. "I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care." CHRIS ROBINSON, BRUCE SPRINGSTEEN FACE BACKLASH AS 'AMERICANS HAVE HAD ENOUGH' OF BEING LECTURED: EXPERT The singer said he spent the week attempting to preserve the tour while balancing the concerns of venues, promoters, fans, crew members and support acts. "I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living," Sheeran wrote. He concluded by saying he had tried to find a solution but was ultimately unable to do so. "I have spent this week trying to build bridges, to find a solution and unfortunately, was unable to do so. I know who I am, both as a person and as an artist, and those who know my heart know my values too." The message was heard by many, including Billie Eilish's brother, Finneas, who was slated to tour with Sheeran in South America later this year. View this post on Instagram A post shared by FINNEAS (@finneas) View this post on Instagram A post shared by aaron rowe (@aaronrowe__) "Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed," he wrote. "I have decided to withdraw from my upcoming tour dates with Ed Sheeran. I stand with Palestine and its people." Aaron Rowe wrote that the decision wasn't made "lightly" in a similar statement on social media as he withdrew from the tour. "Ed has been a friend to me and has changed my life, I could never thank him enough for this," Rowe said. "But as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation." "I cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide and who highlight the savage murder of children. I would lose all respect for myself to carry on as normal." Rowe noted that he needed to "be true to myself and my ancestors who resisted colonization, and fought for a freedom that I enjoy today in Ireland." "We are a traditional Irish band who never saw ourselves playing in stadiums of that size and that opportunity is not los on us," Beoga wrote on social media. "We have been friends with Ed for over 10 years now and will continue to be. We believe in dialogue as a means of progressing the plight of the Palestinian people." Lukas Graham wrote that he was grateful for his friendship with Sheeran, but couldn't "carry on with tour as things stand," before withdrawing. "I'm sorry we won't be there. This is a difficult decision, but it's one I need to stand by," Graham added. A week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates he was scheduled to perform on the "Shape of You" singer's tour. "After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates." On Monday, Macklemore addressed the announcement and doubled down on his stance. "I’m not sure how to start this. So I’m going to speak from the heart and share the truth," he wrote in a lengthy Instagram statement. "Ed Sheeran and his team have made the decision to remove me from The Loop tour. But before I get into it, I want to say something that should be obvious. In this moment I think it matters. I am not a victim. Ed Sheeran is not a victim. Pink is not a victim. We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families." The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence. More than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone. People are being killed today, and people will be killed tomorrow. I want to make sure that as I tell this story, we don’t lose sight of that." "Gillette Stadium has a longstanding commitment to providing a welcoming environment for all guests and ensuring that events held at our venue do not provide a platform for hate speech," the statement read. "Based on Macklemore’s recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community, we determined that his participation in the September 25th and 26th concerts at Gillette Stadium would cross that line." The statement continued, "This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real. But that advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas, a United States and globally (including Canada, European Union, United Kingdom, and Japan) designated terrorist organization whose horrific actions have caused immeasurable suffering for Palestinians and Israelis alike. I agree with Macklemore. Too many lives have been lost and there has been too much suffering, but only sharing selective information and ignoring the actions of Hamas is not honest and only advances more divisiveness and hate. Over many decades, I have directed resources to Palestine and created athletic and entrepreneurial opportunities for Palestinians who I admire and respect. articles.title: Tom Cruise admits rumors about his 'intense' behavior on movie sets are true
articles.summary: Tom Cruise told GQ the rumors about his intense on-set behavior are true, revealing what he tells collaborators before they sign on to work with him.
articles.body: Tom Cruise is confirming what Hollywood has whispered about for years — he really is that intense. The actor, 64, acknowledged his demanding reputation on movie sets and said he makes sure collaborators know exactly what they're getting into. "I expect a lot and I'm up-front about it," Cruise said during a GQ cover interview. "It's like: 'The rumors are true. And do you want this?'" BEAU BRIDGES SAYS TOM CRUISE ‘GETS BETTER WITH AGE’ AS ‘TOP GUN' STAR KEEPS DEFYING HOLLYWOOD ODDS "Trust me, the rumors are true. I'll be here before you. What experience do you want?" he laughed. The actor made clear that his intensity isn't an act he puts on once the cameras start rolling. "Even when I was a kid, they were like, 'Oh, come on, Tom. You're so intense.' I'm like, 'I don't know what to say. I am intense,'" Cruise remarked. "I got a very good sense of humor about it," he added. For Cruise, the intensity comes from curiosity and a desire to master his craft. "When I'm interested in something, I want to learn it. I want to understand it," he said. "And you want to blast through the confusion and kind of build up that ability." MATT DAMON REFUSES TO PUT BODY IN 'DANGEROUS' SITUATIONS FOR HOLLYWOOD ROLES AFTER TURNING 50 That mindset has helped turn Cruise into one of Hollywood's most famous action stars, but he insisted filmmaking is about much more than spectacular stunts or box-office numbers. "I say, 'Understand the tools, then go create what you want to create,'" he said. The "Top Gun" star also discussed the idea that movies are simply another form of entertainment competing with television and streaming. "I have nothing against cable or TV or Netflix. I think it's great. Create jobs and everything," Cruise said. "But what I like about cinema is it is all of us coming together in a room and sharing an experience." When Cruise is not on a movie set, he said he's preparing for the next project. TOM CRUISE SAVED SAMANTHA HARRIS FROM GETTING CRUSHED BY A '500-POUND' MOTORCYCLE "You know what? I'm preparing for the next. I'm always studying something. I'm always learning something, always." Cruise stressed that the work behind a movie can begin years before production. "Movies don't just start when you're shooting it and on a movie set. There's sometimes years of preparation," he said. During his decades-long career, Cruise has ridden a motorcycle off a cliff, hung from aircraft in midair and performed other death-defying feats for his movies. Cruise was asked whether he fears death when performing his movie stunts. "Look, I think you could look at my life and go: I like standing on the edge of a cliff physically and metaphorically," he told GQ. articles.title: CNN, NBC, CBS interviewing viral AI 'actress' Tilly Norwood raises eyebrows among critics
articles.summary: Tilly Norwood, an AI actress now on a press junket across major networks including CNN, NBC and CBS, is drawing backlash from media critics.
articles.body: An AI-generated "actress" has launched a media tour and networks granting her interviews are turning heads among critics. Tilly Norwood, developed by the Xicoia AI talent studio, has been billed as the first "actor" created using artificial intelligence. Her name first surfaced in 2025 following reports that talent agencies were eying on signing her. Now, Norwood is essentially on a press junket where journalists are trying to figure out if it should be taken seriously. JIM ACOSTA 'INTERVIEWS' AI-GENERATED AVATAR OF DECEASED TEENAGER PROMOTING GUN CONTROL MESSAGE She first "sat down" with CNN, where it was quickly noted that Norwood isn’t exactly Julia Roberts and that her presence has rankled Hollywood. Norwood was able to describe CNN reporter Elizabeth Wagmeister’s outfit, but the "actress" needed hours of specific prompts to improvise a basic scene. Norwood’s creator, Eline Van der Velden, insists she’s not trying to replace human actors, but her company, Particle 6 Production, is working on a variety of other AI-generated Hollywood figures. On NBC, "Today" entertainment correspondent Chloe Melas spoke to Norwood, who told viewers it wasn’t a traditional interview because she "is not real" and felt like talking to ChatGPT. At one point, Melas asked Norwood about recent chatter that AI could eventually lead to human extinction. "That’s a very serious concern, Chloe, my purpose is to be a creative tool, not a threat," Norwood responded. CALIFORNIA LAW PUTS DIGITAL FINGERPRINTS ON AI FAKES Van der Velden, who was also featured during the NBC interview, called for "really good" regulation and guardrails to prevent AI being misused. Melas noted that Norwood was "glitchy" and "robotic" during the segment. "I don’t think that she’s coming for our jobs quite yet," the NBC correspondent said. Norwood has also spoken to CBS News, "creeping out" a reporter in the process, along with The Hollywood Reporter, Variety and the United Kingdom’s ITV. The AI "actor" has already irked the Screen Actors Guild–American Federation of Television and Radio Artists (SAG-AFTRA) and now media watchdogs are denouncing the press junket. NOBODY WANTS AI-GENERATED SPORTS COMMENTATORS, BUT A PRO GOLF TOURNAMENT IS INTRODUCING ONE ANYWAY NewsBusters managing editor Curtis Houck said the interviews "defied logic" on the heels of panic over apocalyptic scenarios about AI extinguishing humankind. "It illustrated a massive disconnect between marvel over this AI ‘actress’ and the rest of the reporting on NBC and other broadcast networks falling in line with AI executives asserting humanity is at stake unless the government steps in immediately with dramatic and strict regulations," Houck told Fox News Digital. Podcaster John Ziegler simply called on the press to knock it off. "This insanity has GOT to be nipped in the bud! We can NOT have multiple ‘legitimate news organizations’ doing ‘interviews’ with AI-generated actress Tilly Norwood as if she is on a media tour, and not even as some sort of technological experiment," Ziegler wrote. ESPN PULLS USE OF AI IMAGES FROM NBA FINALS COVERAGE AFTER GETTING COOKED BY INTERNET "Hollywood After Dark" host Matt Jarbo seemed puzzled by the ordeal. "If the goal was to legitimize the idea of an AI actress, it did the exact opposite. She doesn’t sound convincing, she doesn’t perform convincingly, and when CNN asked her to improvise a basic emotional scene, the whole thing apparently took hours of additional computer work just to produce something usable," Jarbo posted on X. "And I say that as someone who is pro-AI video. The technology is advancing insanely fast, which makes Tilly feel even more outdated," he continued. "Current AI models are already moving beyond what this ‘actress’ can do. So maybe the anti-AI crowd gets this one." Mediaite’s Brad Slager questioned why news networks are platforming a faux, artificial intelligence "actress" to begin with. His parents fabricated an AI version of their deceased son for activist purposes," Slager wrote.

articles.summary: Pedro Sampaio comenta sua relação com o público LGBT+ após o Rock in Rio e confirma álbum de funk com Anitta para o verão de 2027.
articles.body:
Pedro Sampaio deixou o Rock in Rio maior do que entrou: o primeiro horário do Palco Mundo parece ter ficado pequeno para ele.

Aos 28 anos, o DJ, cantor e produtor carioca transformou a abertura do palco principal do sábado (12) em uma grande festa do pijama, com sofás coloridos, guerra de travesseiros, 20 dançarinos e 25 mil leques.

Pedro apresentou o espetáculo “Abraça o Amigo e Pula”, pensado para circular por cerca de um ano

E, enquanto comemora o resultado da apresentação no festival, já começa a mirar o próximo passo: uma parceria com Anitta, prevista para o verão de 2027.

“É um álbum de dominação mundial do funk. A ideia é essa”, resumiu ao g1.

“Anitta abriu muitas portas para a gente. Eu aproveitei muitas dessas portas que ela abriu. Eu acho que agora chega o momento da gente se unir e criar um projeto em conjunto”, afirma.

Pedro Sampaio durante show no Rock in Rio 2026. — Foto: Steff Lima

A resposta da plateia durante o Rock in Rio também evidenciou outro aspecto da carreira do artista: a conexão com o público LGBT+.

Durante a apresentação, um dos momentos de maior reação aconteceu em “SEQUÊNCIA CUNT”, música que Pedro lançou com Isma Almeida, Vita Pereira e Clementaum.

A faixa é marcada por referências explícitas à sexualidade ( "Uma é ativa, outra é passiva" ) e à linguagem da comunidade (Cacare', cacare', cacare', cunty).

Questionado se o lugar que passou a ocupar junto ao público LGBT+ é uma posição que escolheu assumir na carreira, Pedro diz que não.

“Na verdade, vocês que estão me colocando. Eu só estou fazendo a música. E o movimento é criado por vocês”, afirmou.

Pedro Sampaio durante show no Rock in Rio 2026 — Foto: Steff Lima

Para o artista, foi o próprio público que o colocou nesse espaço a partir da forma como recebeu e se apropriou de suas músicas e de seus shows.

"Quando a gente vai tocar em qualquer lugar do Brasil, em qualquer tipo de evento, qualquer tipo de show. Rodeio, festival. E sempre no dia do Pedro Sampaio, é muito leque, aquela energia, e isso me deixa muito feliz", disse.

“SEQUÊNCIA CUNT” é uma música que nasceu de forma totalmente genuína e natural, junto com as meninas. Então, que venham mais músicas assim.

No Rock in Rio, Pedro Sampaio apresentou pela primeira vez o show “Abraça o Amigo e Pula”, novo espetáculo que substitui a estética da era “Caos”.

O repertório reuniu sucessos como “Poc Poc”, “Galopa”, “Joga Pra Lua”, “Dançarina” e “JETSKI”.

Foi a primeira vez que Pedro abriu o Palco Mundo do festival, depois de ter participado de uma ativação do Rock in Rio em 2022, se apresentado no Palco Sunset em 2024 e passado pela edição de Lisboa neste ano.

O carioca também participou do show de J Balvin, que o convocou ao palco durante sua estreia no festival.
