articles.title: Ed Sheeran: Entenda confusão envolvendo o cantor e discurso pró-Palestina em show de abertura | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão de afastar rapper gerou reação em cadeia de músicos convidados, deixando turnê sem atrações de abertura.
articles.summary: Decisão de afastar rapper gerou reação em cadeia de músicos convidados, deixando turnê sem atrações de abertura.
articles.body:
Ed Sheeran se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Leo Franco/AgNews

O cantor Ed Sheeran se viu no centro de uma polêmica em torno de sua turnê "Loop" após um discurso pró-Palestina do rapper Macklemore.

Tudo começou no dia 4 de setembro. Segundo o jornal "The Guardian", o rapper americano, que fazia o show de abertura no MetLife Stadium, em Nova Jersey (EUA), gritou "Free Palestine" (Palestina Livre, em tradução literal) . Ele também afirmou que queria que as pessoas em Gaza e na Cisjordânia soubessem que não haviam sido esquecidas.

A declaração motivou uma petição do Conselho Israelense-Americano (Israeli American Council) pedindo a exclusão do rapper da turnê.

A Messina Touring Group, promotora responsável pela etapa dos Estados Unidos da turnê de Sheeran, informou à revista "Rolling Stone" que Macklemore não faria os shows das datas restantes .

"Como promotora da turnê 'Loop' de Ed Sheeran nos Estados Unidos, fomos informados pelos locais que sediarão as próximas datas da turnê de que eles não permitirão a realização dos shows com Macklemore no line-up. Isso resultaria no cancelamento da turnê e impactaria centenas de milhares de fãs. Após discussões com as partes envolvidas, Macklemore não se apresentará nas datas restantes como atração de apoio."

O rapper estava escalado para abrir oito dos dez shows restantes da turnê pelos EUA , com retomada prevista para 19 de setembro na Filadélfia. As cidades com locais de apresentação que teriam se oposto ao retorno de Macklemore incluem Boston, Atlanta, Charlotte, Indianápolis, Dallas e Tampa.

Macklemore canta durante show no Lollapalooza 2019 — Foto: Fábio Tito/G1

O cantor divulgou um longo comunicado na segunda-feira (14) sobre sua saída da turnê.

"Antes de começar, quero dizer algo que deveria ser óbvio. Neste momento, acho que isso importa. Eu não sou uma vítima", escreveu Macklemore no Instagram.

"Temos carreiras, dinheiro, oportunidades, segurança e público no mundo todo. Quaisquer que sejam as consequências que enfrentemos pelo que dizemos, podemos voltar para casa e para nossas famílias. As vítimas são os palestinos."

Já Ed Sheeran afirmou que a decisão partiu da promotora da turnê , a Messina Touring Group.

"Não sou cúmplice. Tenho minhas visões pessoais sobre esse conflito devastador. Só porque eu escolho não falar publicamente, não significa que eu não as tenho, e não significa que eu não me importe", publicou Sheeran.

Um comitê de investigação contratado pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) apontou em junho que Israel alvejou crianças deliberadamente na Faixa de Gaza. Segundo a comissão, tais práticas em Gaza configuram genocídio, crimes contra a humanidade e crimes de guerra.

O relatório da comissão da ONU afirmou ainda que cerca de 30% dos 73 mil mortos na guerra em Gaza eram crianças, pouco mais de 20 mil em números absolutos.

Ed Sheeran se apresenta no Rock in Rio 2024 — Foto: Gustavo Wanderley/g1

Os cantores Finneas, Aaron Rowe e Lukas Graham e a banda Beoga declararam nesta terça-feira (15) que não vão mais abrir os shows de Ed Sheeran .

Com isso, Sheeran perdeu todos os artistas de abertura de sua série de concertos , que tem datas previstas até 11 de dezembro.

Finneas, aliás, abriria as apresentações do cantor britânico em São Paulo nos dias 5 e 6 de dezembro . O grupo Beoga, além de abrir shows, também se apresentava ao lado de Sheeran em trechos de repertório influenciados pela música tradicional irlandesa.

Junto à decisão de cancelamento, os três cantores e o grupo manifestaram apoio à causa palestina.

"Artistas não devem ser silenciados por se manifestar contra a opressão", escreveu Finneas no Instagram.

"Deveríamos poder falar sobre guerra, sobre civis sendo mortos, sobre crianças que merecem crescer. Onde quer que vivam. Qualquer que seja a sua bandeira", afirmou Graham.

"Como irlandeses, conhecemos bem até demais genocídio, fome forçada e ocupação violenta", disse Rowe.

"Somos irlandeses que entendem colonialismo. Como membros fundadores do movimento Artistas Irlandeses pela Palestina, somos ativistas com compromisso pela justiça e continuaremos a ser", publicou a banda Beoga.

Sheeran ainda não comentou a saída dos demais artistas da turnê.

articles.title: Martinho da Vila tem razão em rejeitar junção de sambas-enredo, pois gênero é arte, não peça na máquina do Carnaval | G1
articles.body:
Ao rejeitar união de dois sambas-enredo, Martinho da Vila prova amor à escola que traz no sobrenome artístico desde os anos 1960 — Foto: Leo Aversa / Divulgação

♬ A confusão em torno da escolha do samba-enredo com o qual a escola Unidos de Vila Isabel irá disputar o Carnaval de 2027 – com enredo baseado no livro “Torto arado” (2019), do escritor Itamar Vieira Junior – mostra como as agremiações vem atravessando o samba nesse quesito tão importante na hora do desfile.

Na disputa para eleger o samba campeão, travada no sábado, 12 de setembro, a diretoria da Vila Isabel escolheu o campeão ao juntar dois sambas. Precisamente, o refrão da composição de Paulo César Feital, Danilo Garcia, Júlio Alves, Marcelo Martins, Gabriel Simões, Gustavinho Oliveira e Thales Nunes foi acoplado a outro samba, o assinado por Martinho da Vila – Presidente de Honra da escola e autor de sambas-enredo antológicos desde a segunda metade dos anos 1960 – com André Diniz e Evandro Bocão.

A questão é que Martinho, em nome da arte de fazer samba, desafinou o coro dos contentes e protestou contra a junção dos dois sambas. Diante da importância e do prestígio do compositor fluminense, que exigiu a retirada do nome dele do samba resultante da junção, a diretoria da Unidos de Vila Isabel voltou atrás e em reunião feita na segunda-feira, 14 de setembro, desfez a junção dos sambas-enredo, elegendo campeão somente o samba de autoria da trinca encabeçada por Martinho.

A reversão provocou revolta na ala de compositores do outro samba. Paulo César Feital adotou discurso mais diplomático, defendendo a junção, mas acatando a decisão da diretoria da Vila Isabel. Já Gabriel Simões, Gustavinho Oliveira e Thales Nunes protestaram, revoltados, cogitando inclusive sair da escola.

Egos à parte, Martinho da Vila está coberto de razão. Samba-enredo é arte, não uma peça na engrenagem empresarial do Carnaval carioca. Aceitar a junção – prática que nos últimos anos vem se tornando recorrente nas escolas, diga-se – seria assinar embaixo dessa forma mais fria e racional de formatar samba-enredo.

Foi-se o tempo que um, dois ou três compositores se juntavam para fazer um samba para a escola do coração. Hoje existem os chamados escritórios de samba-enredo, empresas que agregam vários compositores em processo industrial de criação de sambas para várias escolas.

E, pior, nem todos os nomes creditados como autores de um samba-enredo são de fato os compositores desse samba. É até comum que também assinem os sambas aqueles que investem (dinheiro) na criação e promoção do samba até a final – um investimento custoso, diga-se, porque a produção envolve até o transporte e a arregimentação de torcidas organizadas para apoiar determinado samba-enredo na hora da disputa.

Martinho da Vila é de outro tempo de fazer samba, um tempo mais romântico. Martinho é de outros Carnavais. Por isso, que ninguém espere o aval do autor de obras-primas do gênero – como “Quatro séculos de modas e costumes” (1968), “Yayá do Cais Dourado” (1969), “Onde o Brasil aprendeu a liberdade” (1972), “Sonho de um sonho” (1980) e “Pra tudo se acabar na quarta-feira” (1984) – para essa forma empresarial de compor e promover samba-enredo.

Martinho é realmente da Vila. Veste a camisa da escola. Ao rejeitar com razão a junção dos sambas, por pensar o samba-enredo como arte, e não como mera peça na máquina empresarial do Carnaval, Martinho prova ser mais do que nunca da Vila Isabel.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Passinho do Jamal invade o Rock in Rio e conquista Felix, do Stray Kids, Zara Larsson e mais | G1
articles.standfirst: Artistas brasileiros e internacionais replicaram a dança criada pelo recifense Romero Júnior, de 25 anos, que ganhou os camarins e os palcos do festival.
articles.summary: Artistas brasileiros e internacionais replicaram a dança criada pelo recifense Romero Júnior, de 25 anos, que ganhou os camarins e os palcos do festival.
articles.body:
Felix, do Stray Kids, Zara Larsson, Ivete Sangalo e outros artistas entraram na dança durante o Rock in Rio 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/Globoplay, Multishow e redes sociais.

O passinho do Jamal, criado pelo recifense Romero Júnior, ganhou os palcos e camarins do Rock in Rio 2026.

Até então conhecido principalmente pelas coreografias que viralizam nas redes, Romero agora também tenta se firmar como cantor, mas foi a dança que chamou a atenção de artistas brasileiros e internacionais durante o festival.

Felix, do Stray Kids, Zara Larsson, Ivete Sangalo e os bailarinos do espetáculo “Keep Art Human”, de Alok , entraram na brincadeira e reproduziram a coreografia. A seguir, veja os vídeos.

Felix foi um dos integrantes do Stray Kids a entrar na onda durante a passagem do grupo pelo Rock in Rio. Depois de fechar o Palco Mundo na noite de sábado (12), cada integrante fez uma pequena dancinha ou brincadeira diante das câmeras antes de deixar o palco.

Em entrevista ao g1 depois do show, ele contou que tem ouvido bastante baile funk e citou especificamente o “Jamal Dance” entre as tendências brasileiras que chamaram sua atenção.

“Tenho ouvido muito ‘baile funk’ e ‘The Jamal Dance’. Tenho ouvido muito esse gênero. Está muito nos trends e eu acho que é muito divertido”, disse.

O Stray Kids fez história ao ser o primeiro grupo de K-pop a ocupar o posto de headliner do Palco Mundo.

A sueca Zara Larsson também mostrou que entrou no clima brasileiro antes mesmo de subir ao palco.

No camarim do Rock in Rio, a cantora gravou um vídeo para o TikTok fazendo o passinho do Jamal ao som de “Ela Quer Leitada”, faixa que viralizou nas redes.

O vídeo rapidamente ganhou repercussão e já ultrapassou 6,7 milhões de visualizações. Horas depois, Zara fechou a programação do Palco Sunset no último dia do festival, domingo (13).

No domingo (13), foi a vez de Ivete Sangalo levar o passinho para o Palco Mundo.

A cantora abriu a programação do palco principal sob forte chuva e, em meio aos sucessos do repertório, também arriscou a coreografia que tomou conta das redes.

Ivete ainda fez o “six-seven” durante a apresentação e recebeu as filhas Helena e Marina no palco.

O passinho do Jamal também apareceu no espetáculo “Keep Art Human”, de Alok, no Palco Mundo do Rock in Rio, em 11 de setembro.

Os 45 bailarinos que integram a apresentação do DJ entraram na trend e reproduziram a coreografia durante o show no Palco Mundo.

Idealizado por Alok, o projeto defende o valor da criatividade e da expressão humanas em um cenário cada vez mais impactado pela inteligência artificial.

No Rock in Rio, a proposta ganhou forma em uma apresentação que combinou música eletrônica, dança e tecnologia, mas também encontrou espaço para uma das coreografias que mais viralizam nas redes brasileiras.

articles.title: Ariana ou Miley no Rock in Rio? A teoria (negada pelo festival) de que último dia seria 'dia delas' | G1
articles.standfirst: Roberta Medina explicou ao g1 que ideia não faz sentido e citou artistas masculinos em palcos paralelos. Dia com Halsey, Marina Sena, Ivete e Zara Larsson pedia headliner mulher?
articles.summary: Roberta Medina explicou ao g1 que ideia não faz sentido e citou artistas masculinos em palcos paralelos. Dia com Halsey, Marina Sena, Ivete e Zara Larsson pedia headliner mulher?
articles.body:
Uma teoria da conspiração tomou conta das redes sociais durante o Rock in Rio, que aconteceu entre 4 e 13 de setembro. A teoria apontava que a última noite seria um novo dia exclusivo para mulheres, o que faria sentido. Afinal, o dia delas da edição anterior foi um sucesso. De novo, a escalação final seria dominada por cantoras, mas uma mudança de rota alterou o topo do cartaz do Palco Mundo.

O line-up do dia 13 acabou marcado por Ivete Sangalo, Lola Young, Halsey, Marina Sena, Zara Larsson e… Twenty One Pilots , uma dupla de músicos. O Rock in Rio 2026 foi a primeiro desde 2001 sem mulheres anunciadas como headliners do palco principal , contando que Lady Gaga cancelou sua vinda em 2027 e foi substituída pelo Maroon 5.

Para quem especulava o repeteco feminino, a vice-presidente do festival tratou de negar, em entrevista ao g1.“Eu vou dar uma contrariada na lenda, porque a gente anuncia primeiro o headliner, tá?”, respondeu Roberta Medina.

“Na verdade, só para explicar como é que funciona a contratação: começa no headliner. Porque ele é normalmente o artista que move mais pessoas e ele, a partir daí a gente tem o perfil do dia mais ou menos desenhado e a gente vai compondo os outros palcos. Então não confirma. E a gente tem John Summit, Dennis, a gente tem homens incríveis também compondo, né? Então, não foi este caso”, disse citando nomes masculinos de palcos como Espaço Favela e New Dance Order.

Ariana Grande em imagem de divulgação do disco 'Petal' (2026) — Foto: Divulgação

Por outro lado, Roberto Medina deu a entender, em entrevista ao jornal O Globo, que Miley Cyrus teria recusado de última hora ser atração do Rock in Rio. Ele não especificou em qual dia a diva americana cantaria.

Imaginar as duas cantoras como headliners esbarra no momento da carreira delas. Miley dissenão ter vontade de embarcar em longas turnês e prefere se manter longe das superproduções por enquanto. Ariana Grande, além de focar suas energias na carreira de atriz, encerrou sua enxuta "Eternal Sunshine Tour". A série de shows se limitou a 41 datas em arenas dos Estados Unidos, Canadá e Reino Unido, antes de uma pausa para focar em sua vida pessoal.

O impacto de não ter uma estrela pop fechando o festival recaiu sobre o Twenty One Pilots, que pareceu um pouco deslocado no line-up. Sem o peso e o encaixe temático de uma atração como Ariana Grande, a banda liderada por Tyler Joseph e Josh Dun tocou para a menor plateia de headliner desta edição.

O show foi vigoroso e mostrou o amadurecimento deles, mas isso não diminuiu a ingrata tarefa de entregar o seu rap rock e estilos misturados a um público que talvez esperasse uma noite mais pop. Isso, claro, sem contar os fãs do duo americano.

articles.summary: The recent public appearances of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and actor Vijay and actress Trisha Krishnan have once again attracted attention on social m.
articles.body: The recent public appearances of Tamil Nadu Chief Minister and actor Vijay and actress Trisha Krishnan have once again attracted attention on social media. The two were spotted together at Ajith Kumar’s Le Mans Cup race at Silverstone in the UK, where Vijay flagged off the event. Videos from the venue showed Vijay and Trisha watching the race, leading to renewed discussions about their long-standing friendship.Ambika says Trisha should be careful about public appearances with VijayAmid the ongoing discussion, veteran actress Ambika has shared her views on Vijay and Trisha’s friendship. Speaking in an interview with RedPix, she said that a friendship should not automatically be given another meaning simply because one person has reached a higher position. Ambika explained that she would personally avoid situations that could invite negative comments about a close friend who holds an important position. She said, “If I were in Trisha’s place, and I knew that negative criticism would come, I would avoid going along. This is my opinion. We should value friendship, but we should also be careful.”Ambika on Vijay and Trisha: ‘Don’t give friendship another colour’Ambika also stressed that people cannot simply end a friendship because one person has moved into a more prominent position. She said, “When two people are friends, if one of them reaches a higher position in life, we cannot reject that friendship. We should not give it another colour. We can say what we would do in such a situation, but we cannot tell someone else what they should or should not do.” She added that if her presence with a friend in a particular place could lead to unnecessary criticism, she would choose not to attend. Her comments come at a time when Vijay and Trisha’s appearances together are receiving considerable online attention.Vijay and Trisha’s long cinema association continues to draw attentionVijay and Trisha have shared a long professional association, beginning with ‘Ghilli’ in 2004 and continuing with films including ‘Thirupaachi,’ ‘Aathi,’ ‘Kuruvi,’ and ‘Leo.’ Their off-screen appearances have also often become a talking point among fans. articles.body: Katrina Kaif’s recent appearance at a star-studded Ganpati celebration in Mumbai city has sparked a discussion on social media, with some users commenting on the actress’ appearance and postpartum body.Katrina Kaif's rare public appearance sparks debateThe actress, who welcomed her first child, baby Vihaan Kaushal, with husband Vicky Kaushal, in November 2025, largely kept her personal life private since embracing motherhood. Her rare public appearance at the starry event, went viral on social media, prompting a range of reactions to her appearance.While some netizens resorted to trolling the actress, comparing her postpartum look to her appearances in special dance numbers, several fans stepped in to call out what they described as ‘insensitive’ comments.Fans defend Katrina KaifFans took to social media to remind users that pregnancy and motherhood can bring about ‘natural physical and emotional changes’. Coming to Katrina’s defence, they called out what they described as ‘unnecessary scrutiny of a woman’s body’, particularly in the months following childbirth.One fan wrote, "She became a mother less than a year ago, yet some people are already judging her against how she looked years ago. Bodies change. Faces age. Motherhood changes people too. After more than two decades in the spotlight, maybe the most refreshing thing is seeing Katrina look comfortable being herself rather than trying to freeze time."Another fan slammed comments suggesting that the actress was ‘finished’ because of changes to her appearance, writing, "Calling Katrina Kaif ‘finished’ because of postpartum weight gain just exposes you as a sore loser. She’s running a 400 crore beauty empire, embraced motherhood with a beautiful baby, has a happy family, and is gearing up to return to films. That’s success stacked higher than the insecurities of anyone trying to drag her down."Netizens call out double standards Several users also pointed to the contrasting expectations placed on women during pregnancy and after childbirth. Recalling the online chatter around Deepika Padukone’s pregnancy, one user wrote, "mind you when Deepika was pregnant with Dua she was pinned for faking her pregnancy cuz apparently no pregnant woman look “that fit” in their third trimester - now they're crucifying another successful woman cuz she gained few kilos post partum. woman really can never have it all"Another post highlighted, "A woman's body undergoes numerous natural changes throughout the various stages of life and motherhood. Mocking anyone online based on their weight or appearance is simply insensitive. To me, those who engage in such mockery come across as the most despicable and crude people in the world! Whether it is Katrina Kaif or any other woman, physical changes deserve respect. Stop body-shaming; true beauty lies in a serene countenance, self-confidence, and dignity."Fans say postpartum is a 'journey and not a contest'Several fans stressed that postpartum recovery was a 'journey' and not a 'contest'. They tweeted, "Becoming a mother is not easy. I fail to understand why people are so concerned about Katrina Kaif’s looks. Motherhood changes everything: your body, hormones, emotions and energy. Every mother deserves time, space, and compassion to heal. Postpartum is a journey, not a beauty contest."Another social media user wrote, "I tell u what happened. She got married to the man she loves, delivered a beautiful baby and she’s happy as an actress and mother now. While you are ragebaiting here." Another further commented, "A woman’s body undergoes massive changes during and after pregnancy; she’s a new mother at 40 and still looks stunning, unlike the incels hiding behind fake profile pictures. Being a celebrity doesn’t make her immune to natural changes. What a pathetic display of frustration from miserable nobodies."Another user addressed the wider expectations placed on women, writing, "Women’s bodies go through pregnancy, hormones, ageing, stress, recovery and a thousand things men will never understand.Yet somehow, men are always the first to lecture women on how they should look. Calling Katrina Kaif “finished” because her body changed isn’t an opinion. It’s ignorance dressed up as entitlement."Fans hail Katrina Kaif's 'glow'Meanwhile, several fans chose to post more positive messages for the mom of one saying, "She has glow of motherhood and looking so graceful. Too bad you are not able to see." Another said, "People who are body shaming Katrina have no idea what it feels like to become a mother."On the work front, Katrina has not yet announced her next film project. articles.title: Franco Colapinto se moja y elige entre 'El Hormiguero' y 'La Revuelta': "Prefiero que sean personas y no peluches"
articles.standfirst: El piloto argentino de Fórmula 1 fue el segundo invitado de la semana en el programa de David Broncano
articles.summary: El piloto argentino de Fórmula 1 fue el segundo invitado de la semana en el programa de David Broncano
articles.body: Este martes, 15 de septiembre, ‘La Revuelta’ volvió una vez más al ‘access prime time’ de La 1 de RTVE con David Broncano al frente. En esta ocasión, el invitado del espacio del ente público en el Teatro Albéniz fue Franco Colapinto, piloto argentino de Alpine, que corrió este pasado fin de semana en el GP de España de Madrid, logrando una séptima posición. Así le dio la bienvenida el presentador: “Es de los mejores pilotos del mundo, es un fenómeno, un aplauso para un chico que parece que tiene 13 años”. Asimismo, el piloto entró entre risas y reveló que el presentador le había dicho que no había visto una carrera de F1 en su vida. Del mismo modo, el argentino comentó que había “atrasado su vuelo” para venir al programa al haberse “conocido” en un evento en la mañana de este martes. Broncano le agradeció el gesto y le instó a hablar de F1, negándose el invitado a ello: “Ya hablamos demasiado antes”, respondió. Por otro lado, salió a escena la rivalidad con ‘El Hormiguero’, incidiendo el presentador en que ganaron en número de espectadores el lunes, 14 de septiembre, pero no en porcentaje de share. Fue aquí cuando Broncano pidió que sacaran los datos de cuando fue Colapinto al programa de Motos hace dos años, superando en aquel entonces ‘La Revuelta’ a ‘El Hormiguero’. Colapinto se interesó por saber cuál era el nombre de Grison y Ricardo Castella, añadiendo lo siguiente: “Prefiero que sean personas y no peluches”. Luego, tuvo el tradicional intercambio de regalos entre presentador e invitado, pero él no le trajo nada, alegando que le iba a regalar un casco, tirando de ironía: “A Motos sí, pero a ti, no”. David se echó las manos a la cabeza y las risas se desataron en el plató de ‘La Revuelta’. Prosiguieron hablando de F1, una profesión que para Colapinto es “un sueño” y el comunicador del ente público se interesó acerca de si alguno del paddock se ponía bótox o pelo, algo que sentenció el invitado así: “Alguno se habrá puesto pelo, bótox no sé qué es”. Cambiando de tema, Colapinto reveló que se vino a Europa con 14 años, concretamente a Italia, a vivir a un taller y su padre tuvo que vender su casa para que él corriera en Fórmula 4 a los 15 años. Para finalizar, intentó esquivar las preguntas clásicas del programa, justificándolo así: “Es por lo único que no venía”. Sin embargo, sí que respondió a la de relaciones sexuales: “Estuve con muchas carreras. Yo tengo al que me maneja parte deportiva, Fernando Belasteguín me dice que está prohibido acabar en fin de semana de carreras porque baja la testosterona y rindes menos”.

articles.title: Aitana sorprende a sus fans subiendo a Plex al escenario en su último concierto de Madrid: "Parece que me caso..."
articles.standfirst: Continúa su gira 'Cuarto Azul World Tour' por España, América y Europa
articles.summary: Continúa su gira 'Cuarto Azul World Tour' por España, América y Europa
articles.body: Aitana ha puesto este martes, 15 de septiembre, el punto final a sus cuatro conciertos consecutivos en el Movistar Arena de Madrid con una noche marcada por las sorpresas. La cantante, que ha conseguido colgar el cartel de sold out en las cuatro fechas madrileñas, cerró su paso por la capital con uno de los momentos más comentados de su 'Cuarto Azul World Tour': la aparición de Plex sobre el escenario durante 'Superestrella'. La artista ya había convertido Madrid en una de las grandes paradas de su gira. Las actuaciones del 11, 12, 14 y 15 de septiembre agotaron sus localidades, después de que Aitana también llenara las cuatro fechas programadas en el Palau Sant Jordi de Barcelona. En total, la gira había superado las 450.000 entradas vendidas en España, según los datos difundidos por Universal Music. La última noche en la capital tuvo, además, un componente especialmente personal. Aitana apareció vestida completamente de blanco y, en un momento del espectáculo, hizo referencia al aspecto nupcial de su estilismo ante el público: "Hoy vengo de blanco, parece que me caso. Es broma. De momento no". Cuando llegó 'Superestrella', una de las canciones más reconocibles de la actual etapa de Aitana, la cantante sorprendió a los asistentes al subir a Plex al escenario. El creador de contenido, vestido también totalmente de blanco, apareció junto a ella mientras el público reaccionaba con gritos y ovaciones. Aitana le cantó parte del tema y ambos compartieron el escenario ante un Movistar Arena completamente entregado. La aparición no era completamente inédita dentro de la gira, ya que Plex ya había salido al final del 'hit' en algunos conciertos pero nunca había participado en la coreografía. Aunque Madrid ya ha quedado atrás, Aitana todavía tiene dos conciertos pendientes en España antes de comenzar la siguiente fase internacional de la gira. La cantante actuará los próximos 18 y 19 de septiembre en el Bizkaia Arena BEC! de Bilbao. La primera de las dos fechas figura como agotada, mientras que la segunda continúa apareciendo en la web oficial de la artista con entradas disponibles. Después llegará el salto internacional. La primera parada será Bogotá, el 16 de octubre, seguida de Santiago de Chile, el 19 de octubre. La gira continuará después por Argentina, donde Aitana tiene previstas tres actuaciones en Buenos Aires los días 21, 22 y 23 de octubre. El tramo americano seguirá en México con conciertos en Monterrey (28 de octubre), Guadalajara (30 de octubre) y Querétaro (31 de octubre). En noviembre será el turno de Ciudad de México, con actuaciones previstas los días 5, 6 y 7 de noviembre en el Auditorio Nacional. Dos de esas tres fechas, la del 6 y la del 7, aparecen actualmente como agotadas en la página oficial de la gira. La gira cruzará después el Atlántico rumbo a Estados Unidos. Aitana actuará en Nueva York el 27 de noviembre, en el Brooklyn Paramount, una cita que figura como sold out, y dos días después, el 29 de noviembre, en Miami, en The Fillmore Miami Beach. Y todavía quedará una última etapa europea. En 2027, 'Cuarto Azul World Tour' llegará a Lisboa (30 de enero), Milán (6 de febrero), Londres (12 y 13 de febrero) y París (20 de febrero). De esta forma, el concierto del 15 de septiembre en Madrid no solo ha servido para cerrar una de las etapas españolas más multitudinarias de la gira, sino también para dejar una de las imágenes más personales de su paso por la capital: Aitana, vestida de blanco, bromeando con una posible boda y terminando 'Superestrella' junto a Plex ante un pabellón completamente entregado.

El monólogo continuó. “Algunos de los hombres de esta categoría practican la actuación del método y otros actúan de forma normal, menos molesta”. Y siguió: “Pero, sea como sea, cuando estos chicos dan en el clavo, se saben todas sus líneas. ¿Por qué? Porque empezaron a mirar sus guiones esa misma mañana”. Seguidamente recordó unas manifestaciones del rapero DJ Khaled, y cuando estas fueron sujeto de la censura. “Creo que fue DJ Khaled quien dijo ‘los hombres de verdad no le hacen sexo oral a su mujer’. articles.body: España ya tiene representante para los Oscar toda vez la Academia de Cine lo ha comunicado esta misma mañana. La bola negra, la nueva película de Los Javis, será la candidata española a la estatuilla a Mejor película internacional, y eso si no acaba estando nominada a alguna otra categoría, como todo hace indicar. El dúo formado por Javier Calvo y Javier Ambrossi atrae muchas miradas en su trayectoria internacional, y ahora apunta a Hollywood. Se trata de un reto más. Así lo ha comunicado el presidente de la Academia, Fernando Méndez-Leite, que ha contado con la presencia del director Alejandro Amenábar, y ha sido el encargado de hacer oficial el anuncio. 'La bola negra' competía con 'El ser querido', la película de Rodrigo Sorogoyen con Javier Bardem y Victoria Luengo como protagonistas, y con 'Los domingos', la última película de Alauda Ruiz de Azúa, pero finalmente ha resultado agraciada la primera. Gracias en parte a que 'La bola negra' obtuvo el galardón a Mejor dirección ex-aequo con Pawel Pawlikowski por Fatherland en el Festival de cine de Cannes. Dicha película que aspira a la estatuilla versa sobre tres hombres de tres épocas distintas pero conectados por la sexualidad y el deseo, y que además están unidos por un mismo hombre: Federico García Lorca. 'La bola negra' será la representante española y releva a 'Sirat. Trance en el desierto', que fue la película escogida por la Academia para representar a España en los últimos Oscar, celebrados el pasado mes de marzo.

articles.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle switched Archie and Lili's school after just two days, but royal experts say the traffic issues were entirely predictable.
articles.body: None of the security and logistical concerns that forced Prince Harry and Meghan Markle to switch the school their children were attending in England should have been a surprise, according to royal experts. "The logistics haven’t changed since Harry and Meghan plotted their U.K. return," Kinsey Schofield, host of YouTube’s "Kinsey Schofield Unfiltered," told Fox News Digital. "None of this should have come as a surprise." Schofield said that her sources were warning her about the traffic around the school two weeks ago, "before Archie and Lili had even started. When I spoke to people locally, the school-run traffic was one of the very first issues they raised with me." The royal couple moved their family from California to the Cotswolds, outside of London, late last month. PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE’S SCHOOL WARNING LETTERS REIGNITE PRIVACY BATTLE THEY ‘CANNOT CONTROL’: EXPERTS Royal commentator Richard Fitzwilliams agreed that moving Prince Archie and Princess Lillibet to a new school just two days into the term was "extraordinary and smacks of haste and a lack of preparedness by the Sussexes." He added, "If the school run had the problems they have encountered, why did they not know earlier and why wait until their children have actually started school. Why is this all played out in the public domain? Security issues should be private. There will be those who believe it has been handled in this way to increase pressure on the authorities to get automatic security." PRINCE WILLIAM 'NO LONGER RECOGNIZES' PRINCE HARRY AS SECURITY BATTLE LEAVES DUKE 'CLOSE TO TEARS': EXPERT Harry has been advocating for taxpayer-funded security for his family for years after they stepped back as senior royals. "According to my sources, Harry and Meghan and their security experts were concerned about the length of journey and how potential ambush cars could block their way and hijack the children," royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital. "They have been brought closer to their home and the security arrangements are being reviewed." PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE ACCUSED OF SEEKING ‘BEST OF BOTH WORLDS’ WITH UK MOVE: EXPERT "I feel this is a very necessary step and giving Harry and Meghan peace of mind," he added. Fitzwilliams explained that Harry’s request for taxpayer-funded security would involve a detail that is armed and has access to intelligence that his private team doesn’t have. "That is why I find the suggestion that these logistical difficulties only became apparent once the children started school difficult to take seriously." PRINCE HARRY AND MEGHAN MARKLE ARRIVE IN UK WITH KIDS, MARKING DRAMATIC RETURN 6 YEARS AFTER ROYAL EXIT "He has been informed that there will now be a security review for both of them, as they have permanently moved to the U.K.," he continued. "He lost a series of court battles over this but has appealed to the home secretary." Schofield said she had been told the original school had a great reputation with lots of international students, but "navigating the area would be a very big burden for the Sussexes." MEGHAN MARKLE RETURNS TO BRITAIN WITH PRINCE ARCHIE AND PRINCESS LILIBET FOR FIRST TIME IN YEARS "That is why I find the suggestion that these logistical difficulties only became apparent once the children started school difficult to take seriously," she admitted. "Locals knew about the traffic. The Sussexes knew where they were living. They knew the distance to the school. They knew they had two children of different ages who could potentially have different schedules. And, most importantly, they knew the limitations and requirements of their private security operation." Altogether, that could have been a 45-munute commute four times a day, she stressed. "It was always an ambitious school run." "My sympathy is with Archie and Lili," Schofield added. "Thankfully, children are resilient and this happened very early in the term, but ideally these basic practical considerations would have been resolved before they ever walked through the school gates." The last thing these children need after moving countries and changing schools is another unnecessary disruption." But she said the situation "raises legitimate questions" about their strategy. "This wasn’t some obscure problem nobody could have anticipated." PRINCE HARRY, MEGHAN MARKLE’S UK MOVE PUTS FRESH SPOTLIGHT ON THEIR EXPLOSIVE CLAIMS AGAINST ROYAL FAMILY Schofield questioned why their professional security team wasn’t able to identify that problem before the kids started school. "It can be boring, it can be vanilla, but there is something enormously comforting about knowing exactly what you are going to get. They show up, they stick to the program, they honor their commitments and, over time, that reliability creates trust." Podcasts come and go, business relationships change, plans are announced and then abandoned, and now their children’s school has changed after just two days. Individually, there may be perfectly reasonable explanations for each decision, but collectively they create an impression of instability." A spokesperson for the Sussexes told several outlets, "The decision for the children to move schools was taken following a discussion with the family’s security team about the practicalities of their current arrangements. The parents remain extremely grateful to all the teachers and staff for the love, care and effort they have shown their family. This decision should in no way be interpreted as a reflection on the school or the exceptional care the children have received there." Fox News Digital has reached out to Archewell for comment.

articles.title: Prevent RNLI doxxing, Culture Secretary Nandy tells social media sites
articles.summary: Lisa Nandy demands action from social media firms as RNLI volunteers face online abuse.
articles.body:
Social media platforms have been told they must do more to protect people from doxxing and online abuse after personal details of RNLI volunteers were shared online.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy chaired a meeting to challenge firms, including Meta, TikTok, Snap and YouTube owner Google, after lifeboat crews were targeted during anti-migrant protests.

Nandy also wants tech companies to tackle videos that glorify dangerous driving, saying she wants the UK to have the "gold standard" of online spaces.

Meta said it removed content that shared or solicited personal information and prohibited the promotion of high-risk challenges. TikTok, Snap and Google have also been contacted for a comment.

Doxxing is the act of publicly sharing someone's personal information, usually to harass, humiliate or threaten them.

RNLI volunteer lifeboat crews became the target of hostility during recent protests in Dover and Portsmouth and some had their names and photographs shared online.

Nandy said: "I'm appalled, not just by the treatment of charity volunteers who are trying to save lives, but also the treatment of police officers who are being doxxed online, having their names, photos published, there are journalists who had their addresses published - and this has to stop."

Speaking to Times Radio , she said: "I have made a commitment to the RNLI and to, not just charities but public sector workers, police officers and others who are being routinely harassed and abused online in the course of work, that we will tighten up the law.

"All of the different social media companies have completely different terms of service, different standards that they apply to online hatred directed at individuals.

"Some of them will automatically remove that content. Some of them, frankly, won't."

Nandy added that X "didn't even bother to turn up" which she said was "an absolute disgrace".

Nandy told platforms they needed to be quicker, more proactive and more rigorous in removing harmful content.

She said the government "is not neutral on this" and warned she was willing to consider legislation.

Nandy has also written to all RNLI volunteers to condemn the online abuse and reaffirm the government's backing for law enforcement where the content is illegal.

Meta said: "We remove content that shares, offers or solicits personally identifiable information or other private information that could lead to physical harm.

"We prohibit people from promoting, advocating for or encouraging participation in high-risk viral challenges, including the trend of dangerous driving against oncoming traffic.

"We take down this kind of content once we become aware of it."

On 6 September, anti-migrant protesters blocked roads in Portsmouth in an attempt to stop 120 people who arrived at the Eastney Landing ferry port area with the RNLI's assistance.

Footage was subsequently posted on social media showing volunteers of the Poole-based charity labelled as "traitors".

RNLI chief executive Peter Sparkes said: "Recent events have generated deliberate misinformation and a misunderstanding about the RNLI.

"Sadly, as a result, some of our volunteers and staff have been the subject of online and, in the worst cases, physical abuse.

"The RNLI's people represent the very best in our society, they selflessly give up their time to keep others safe."

articles.title: Matthew Rhys was always the Main Man. You just didn’t know it till this year’s Emmys
articles.summary: At the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, Welsh actor Matthew Rhys achieved an unprecedented milestone in modern television history. Winning two Lead Actor a.
articles.body: At the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards, Welsh actor Matthew Rhys achieved an unprecedented milestone in modern television history. Winning two Lead Actor awards in a single evening—one for his portrayal of the unhinged real estate developer Nile Jarvis in Netflix’s limited series The Beast in Me, and another for his performance as an anxious island mayor in Apple TV+’s breakout comedy Widow’s Bay—Rhys secured his place in the industry record books.For the ones who have followed the Welsh actor’s career closely, this hasn’t been a surprise at all. In fact, it is delayed gratification. Matthew Rhys has been the main man for a while now. A lot of people just didn’t notice how much – i.e., just how prolific his career has been since he played one of the brothers in Brothers & Sisters, which premiered 20 years ago. In 2006.Combined with his 2018 Lead Actor in a Drama win for FX's The Americans, Rhys became the first male actor to win top lead acting honours across all three major television categories: Drama, Comedy, and Limited Series. He also became the first performer ever to collect two lead acting Emmys on the same night.For casual viewers, the double win may have looked like a sudden arrival. But for anyone who has watched Rhys over the past two decades, it feels more like the industry finally catching up with an actor who has been quietly building one of the most interesting careers on television. His achievement is not just about two trophies on one night. It is about the remarkable distance he has travelled as a performer, from a relatively understated supporting player to one of television’s most versatile leading men.From the quiet man to the man who can do almost anythingTo understand why the Emmy sweep matters, let’s look at the journey rather than just the destination. Before the chaos of Widow’s Bay or the menace of The Beast in Me, Rhys built his reputation through performances that depended heavily on restraint, silence and what was happening beneath the surface.His American breakthrough came with Brothers & Sisters, where he played Kevin Walker, a corporate lawyer and one of the members of the complicated Walker family. The role introduced him to a large American television audience and established something that would remain central to his career: the ability to make a character’s pulse in every scene. You didn’t feel it was a performance.Then came The Americans, the role that changed the way audiences saw him. As Philip Jennings, a Soviet spy living undercover in suburban Virginia, Rhys had to play a spy, also a family man, husband and father – a man who had to hide a great deal from everyone. But in that subterfuge was the revelation of Rhys as a consummate actor.Philip could not announce his emotions because the entire character was built around concealment. Much of the performance was therefore in the small details: a pause, a look, a tired posture, a change in his voice — and of course his many disguises (read different wigs).The actor in Rhys made Philip’s exhaustion feel physical. As an audience, you feel you are in his place, feeling and doing everything he does. Even if it’s murder. He was a killer, but he was also a man increasingly uncertain about the life he had chosen.The performance was powerful because of Rhys’ “volatile restraint”. Sounds a bit of an oxymoron, but that was precisely what his eyes conveyed. He rarely pushed it too far. The emotions were often held back, allowing the audience to feel the pressure building underneath. That performance earned him his first Primetime Emmy for Lead Actor in a Drama in 2018.Then came Perry Mason, where Rhys took on a very different version of a familiar character. Instead of the polished courtroom lawyer audiences already knew in Brothers & Sisters or the spy in The Americans, he played Mason as a damaged, brooding private investigator in Depression-era Los Angeles. Some called his character a “loser”. And he played it to perfection. This performance was built around a man carrying considerable emotional weight. Losing more than winning.By this time, there was a pattern emerging. Rhys was becoming exceptionally good at playing complicated men who did not necessarily explain themselves. His characters could be angry, wounded, morally conflicted or exhausted, but the performance rarely told the audience exactly what to feel. Rhys trusted the character and, more importantly, he trusted his audience.And then he changed the rules.Two new characters, two completely different MatthewsThe real surprise of his recent career has been the extent to which Rhys has allowed himself to become unpredictable. In The Beast in Me, he plays Nile Jarvis, a wealthy and intimidating real estate developer, who becomes embroiled in a psychological battle with his neighbour. It is a role that draws on a side of Rhys that audiences had rarely seen. The actor brings a dangerous charisma to Jarvis, making him difficult to read and even harder to trust.The performance has a volatility that is very different from the controlled tension of Philip Jennings. Rhys can suddenly become threatening, aggressive or almost unnervingly charming. This character felt capable of changing direction any moment.At the same time, Widow’s Bay allowed him to go in the opposite direction. As an anxious small-town mayor dealing with a haunted island, Rhys embraces physical comedy, panic and deadpan humour. The character is nervous, overwhelmed and frequently out of control.This is where the Emmy story becomes quite interesting. It is one thing for a dramatic actor to successfully move into comedy. It is quite another to do it while retaining the qualities that made audiences take you seriously in the first place.Rhys does not simply play the mayor for laughs. He finds the fear underneath the comedy. His nervous energy becomes part of the joke, while his timing keeps the character from becoming a caricature. Physical comedy also requires a different kind of confidence because the actor has to be willing to look foolish. And Rhys does it with confidence.The same performer who spent years communicating through a raised eyebrow or a barely audible change in tone was now into physical chaos.The two performances, arriving in the same Emmy cycle, make a larger point about the actor’s career: he was always an actor waiting for television to give him enough room to display his full range.Wales gave him the ear that Hollywood could not hearThere is another part of the Matthew Rhys story that is easy to overlook: his Welsh identity. Born in Cardiff, Rhys grew up speaking Welsh as his first language and attended Welsh-medium schools before studying at RADA in London.His connection to Wales has remained an important part of his identity, even as much of his professional life has unfolded in the US. His Welsh identity gave him something that became extremely useful in Hollywood: an unusually sensitive ear for language.For years, many American viewers simply assumed Rhys was American. His performance as Philip Jennings was so convincing that his real accent became almost irrelevant. He has spoken about modelling his American speech on George Clooney’s voice in ER, and his ability to inhabit American accents has become one of the less visible skills behind his performances.It is easy to forget how much technical work goes into making an accent disappear. An actor is not only changing pronunciation. Rhythm, breathing, pitch and the placement of sounds all have to change. Rhys has made that process look effortless.And yet he has often spoken about accents with a sense of humility, treating them as something that requires constant attention rather than a skill he has completely mastered.Rhys’ greatest strength is that even after decades in the business, he seems more interested in getting the work right than in behaving like someone who has already arrived. “I’ve realized that nobody's going to die if I don't get it right and that there are a number of things out there, beyond acting, that are very interesting and fulfilling,” Rhys had once said in an interview.The career that was built by waitingThere is something old-fashioned about Rhys’s career. He did not become an overnight superstar. He accumulated roles, experience and credibility over time. That is the most important currency in a world that loves and creates overnight stars daily. But Rhys wasn’t one of them. By choice. It wasn’t just every script he chose. An actor’s life is also defined by the roles he doesn’t choose. His grounded Welsh roots never let temptation be the ultimate decider. It was restraint for the actor in terms of his performance. And discerning in terms of roles to pick.Before Brothers & Sisters, there had been years of British television and film work, including The Edge of Love. But Brothers & Sisters gave him global visibility. The Americans gave him prestige. Perry Mason allowed him to carry a darker, more complex series. His latest projects have expanded the range even further.The interesting thing is that Rhys himself has not always seemed convinced that he belongs in the room. He has said so in many interviews. Despite playing powerful, intimidating and emotionally complicated men, he has spoken openly about his own insecurities. He has described himself as a “nervous Nelly” and talked about the identity crisis and lack of confidence that helped push him towards acting in the first place. “I've suffered from an identity crisis my entire life. It's why I went into acting,” he had said.That contrast between the actor and the characters is one of the more fascinating things about him. On screen, he can dominate a room. Off screen, his public persona is often self-deprecating and slightly awkward. His characters may know exactly what they want. The actor has often described himself as someone who worries about saying the wrong thing.Perhaps that is part of why his performances feel so convincing. He does not appear to be playing confidence from a distance. He understands the instability beneath it.His career also suggests that he was never particularly interested in chasing celebrity for its own sake. He kept choosing difficult characters and complicated stories, allowing recognition to build slowly around the work.Television eventually caught up with that strategy. As the medium began to move away from simple heroes and villains towards damaged, contradictory and morally-complicated characters, actors like Rhys had more opportunities to demonstrate what they could do.Seen together, these roles make the Emmy double win easier to understand. They are not variations of the same performance. Each requires a different physicality, rhythm and emotional register. And somewhere underneath all of them is an actor who has spent years learning how little he needs to do to command attention.Range is not necessarily about doing something completely different every time. It is about finding a different truth for every character.Even Hollywood’s “First Family” keeps it privateRhys’s life away from acting has also become part of his public story, particularly his relationship with actress Keri Russell.The couple first met casually before reconnecting while working together on The Americans. They began dating in 2014 and have since built a family life in New York while keeping much of it away from public scrutiny.Their relationship has become a favourite among television audiences partly because of the contrast between their professional visibility and their private approach to fame.That privacy was particularly noticeable during the Emmys. Rhys did not thank Russell during either of his acceptance speeches, something that might have seemed surprising given their history.The reason was simple: Russell had asked him not to.The couple had already joked about the subject during Rhys’s 2018 Emmy acceptance speech, when he teased Russell from the stage. Her reaction became one of the memorable moments of that ceremony.Years later, the joke had evolved into something more meaningful. Rhys respected her wish to keep their private relationship away from the public performance of an awards ceremony.Backstage, however, he was generous in his praise of Russell, calling her a “class act” and speaking warmly about the way she supports other actors. He also revealed that he keeps his Emmy awards in the basement and plans to bring them upstairs when Russell wins one of her own.It is a small detail, but it fits the larger Rhys story. For all the spectacle surrounding awards, fame and television history, he still seems more interested in the people and relationships that exist away from the spotlight.The Emmys did not make Matthew Rhys the main manThe easiest way to look at Rhys’s extraordinary Emmy night is as a breakthrough in terms of record-setting and acting credentials. But that would be misleading. He broke through a long time ago.There is also something satisfying about the timing though. Rhys is not a newcomer suddenly discovering success. He is an actor who has spent two decades working, experimenting, disappearing into characters and letting his career grow at its own pace. Some time ago, in an interview, Rhys had said: “In my twenties, I thought I was Robert De Niro and I invested all of myself in my acting. But as I’ve gotten older, I’ve calmed down a bit. I’ve thrown my game plan out of the window.” Possibly the best decision of his life.And that’s why Matthew Rhys has always been the main man.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Macklemore's long history of controversy from Grammy wins to 'Free Palestine' concert remarks
articles.summary: Macklemore's pro-Palestinian concert remarks and controversial moments long predate his removal from Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour" over his "Hind's Hall" performance.
articles.body: Macklemore's activism began long before his pro-Palestinian plight during Ed Sheeran's "Loop Tour." The musician, who's full name is Ben Haggerty, was kicked off Sheeran's tour following backlash from his "Free Palestine" messaging during his opening act at MetLife Stadium over the weekend. While the fallout continues now that four supporting acts have withdrawn from the tour, Macklemore, 43, is no stranger to controversy and has often used his platform to amplify political issues. ED SHEERAN SAYS HE TRIED TO 'BUILD A BRIDGE' OVER MACKLEMORE TOUR SPOT BEFORE VENUES SAID NO The artist broke into the mainstream music scene in 2012 with the release of "The Heist," his debut studio album as the duo Macklemore & Ryan Lewis. He faced criticism for sweeping the 2014 Grammys with four awards, which included winning the Best Rap Album Grammy over fan favorite Kendrick Lamar, who was equally nominated for seven awards that night. MACKLEMORE DOUBLES DOWN AFTER GETTING KICKED OFF ED SHEERAN TOUR AFTER PRO-PALESTINE STANCE Macklemore reached out to Lamar after the show and shared a screenshot of his text on social media where he told the "Humble" rapper that he was "robbed" of the win. "My text to Kendrick after the show. He deserved best rap album... I'm honored and completely blown away to win anything much less 4 Grammys," Macklemore wrote. "But in that category, he should have won IMO. And that's taking nothing away from The Heist. Just giving GKMC it's proper respect." He added, "With that being said, thank you to the fans. You're the reason we were on that stage tonight. And to play Same Love on that platform was a career highlight. The greatest honor of all. That's what this is about. Progress and art. Thank you." Grammy viewers witnessed Macklemore & Ryan Lewis perform "Same Love" on stage to a mass wedding between 33 same-sex and heterosexual couples, officiated by Queen Latifah. At the end of the performance, Madonna appeared on stage for a rendition of her song, "Open Your Heart." BLACK CROWES FACE BACKLASH AFTER CHRIS ROBINSON SHUTS DOWN U.S.A. CHANT AND CALLS FANS 'IGNORANT' That same year, Macklemore faced backlash following an appearance with Ryan Lewis at The Museum of Pop Culture in Seattle, where he wore a black wig, beard and fake nose, which some claimed was an antisemitic costume. The singer issued an apology shortly after and said that his costume wasn't intended to reflect a caricature of a Jewish man, but that he was trying to disguise himself in the crowd. "Family, friends and fans alike who know me well, know that I'm absolutely not the person described in certain headlines today," he wrote on his website. "There is no worse feeling than being misunderstood, especially when people are hurt or offended." "I respect all cultures and all people," he continued. "I would never intentionally put down anybody for the fabric that makes them who they are. I love human beings, love originality, and ... happen to love a weird outfit from time to time." He also posted on X, "A fake witches nose, wig, and beard = random costume. Not my idea of a stereotype of anybody." In 2023, he was one of many who signed the Arists4Ceasefire letter in support of Palestinian rights and humanitarian aid for Gaza and the following year released "Hind's Hall," an anthem supporting pro-Palestinian student protestors. During a performance at Seattle's Palestine Will Live Forever festival, Macklemore faced heavy criticism after leading an anti-U.S. chant where he encouraged the crowd to say, "F- - - America." "My thoughts and feelings are not always expressed perfectly or politely," he said on social media at the time. "Sometimes I slip up and get caught in the moment. Saturday night was one of those times. PINK HITS BACK AMID BACKLASH FOR CRITICIZING MACKLEMORE'S PRO-PALESTINIAN CONCERT REMARKS He added, "Unfortunately, the historic event in my hometown that brought thousands of people together to raise awareness and money for the people of Palestine has become overshadowed by two words." Macklemore admitted that he "lost endorsements, I've lost shows, I've lost business ties," but that his support remained "unwavering." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "My intent always comes back to the pursuit of peace, love, equality and liberation for all. And that isn’t radical, it’s human. I don’t think I’m alone," he noted. The backlash resulted in Macklemore being dropped from the inaugural Neon City Festival in Las Vegas, Nevada. One week after Macklemore repeatedly called to "Free Palestine" and performed "Hind’s Hall" while opening for Sheeran, the rapper was dropped from the remaining U.S. dates. The "Shape of You" singer said he was "appalled" by the conflict between Israel and Palestine and described the suffering on both sides as "a human tragedy," according to a lengthy statement shared on Instagram after Macklemore accused Sheeran and tour organizers of sidelining him over his pro-Palestinian remarks. Sheeran said he deliberately avoided using his professional platform for politics because his audience includes young people and children from diverse backgrounds. Sheeran said concertgoers attend his shows expecting "a place of safety and sanctuary" rather than a political forum. On Monday, Macklemore claimed that Sheeran told him Robert Kraft, the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, had rallied other stadium owners to oppose allowing the rapper to perform. According to his account, the venues allegedly gave Sheeran an ultimatum: "If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues." articles.title: Quote of the day by Leonardo DiCaprio: 'I just really love doing what I do. I know every career is fleeting and there will be time periods when I don’t get the opportunities...so I am taking advantage of them,' a powerful life lesson on making the most of the present, loving your work and knowing that no career lasts forever
articles.summary: In his powerful quote, Leonardo DiCaprio emphasizes the fleeting nature of careers and the importance of loving what you do. His thoughts provide a valuable perspective on making the most of present opportunities and valuing hard work.
articles.body: A career can look permanent when everything is going well. The projects keep coming, the audience keeps growing and one opportunity seems to lead naturally to another. But for actors, that kind of certainty can disappear just as quickly. Leonardo DiCaprio has experienced both sides of that equation, moving from a teenage actor to one of Hollywood's most sought-after stars while continuing to take on challenging roles.Years into his career, DiCaprio spoke openly about what keeps him motivated. Rather than focusing only on the fruits that his work brings, he focused on his profession. He confessed to genuinely enjoying acting and understanding that opportunities do not last forever. His words offer a different way of looking at success: appreciate the work while you have the chance to do it.Today’s quote of the day by Leonardo DiCaprio reads: “I just really love doing what I do. I know every career is fleeting and there will be time periods when I don’t get the opportunities that I’m getting right now, so I am taking advantage of them.”What does the quote by Leonardo DiCaprio mean?DiCaprio's comment is less about chasing success and more about appreciating the opportunity to work. The actor discussed his motivation during an interview in The Guardian, connected to ‘J. Edgar’, the 2011 film in which he played an FBI director. The key idea is that a career can change at any point. An actor may have several projects lined up today and face a quieter period tomorrow. Rather than expecting good opportunities to keep coming his way, DiCaprio’s comment points to the importance of valuing them while they are there. His love for acting is another important part of what he is saying.How is the quote by Leonardo DiCaprio relevant today?The constant need to achieve more can sometimes make people overlook the work they are already doing. No career stays on the same path forever. There are good phases, slower periods, fresh opportunities and moments when things simply do not go as planned.That is where DiCaprio’s words feel especially relevant. When a good opportunity comes along, it makes sense to give it your full attention rather than taking it for granted. And when you actually enjoy the work, success becomes more than just reaching the next milestone.The idea also extends far beyond the film industry. Someone starting a career, running a business or working in a creative field can face periods when opportunities are abundant and others when they are harder to find. Focusing on what you can do now does not mean forgetting your long-term goals.Early life of Leonardo DiCaprioHe was born on November 11, 1974, in Los Angeles, California. He started looking for acting opportunities when he was still young, appearing in commercials and television shows before making the move to movies. His early film credits included ‘This Boy’s Life’ and ‘What’s Eating Gilbert Grape’. The latter brought him his first Academy Award nomination.Those early performances quickly made it clear that DiCaprio was capable of much more than playing the role of a young Hollywood star. His versatility and dedication earned him respect in the industry.How did Leonardo DiCaprio’s rise to fame?In 1997, 'Titanic' made DiCaprio a global star. He played Jack Dawson in James Cameron’s movie. The film became a global success, and DiCaprio’s performance turned him into one of Hollywood’s most recognisable young actors.Rather than staying with conventional romantic roles, he continued choosing varied projects such as ‘The Beach’, ‘Gangs of New York’, ‘Catch Me If You Can’, ‘The Aviator’, ‘The Departed’, ‘Inception’ and ‘Django Unchained’.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: After slamming 'Dhurandhar' for recreating old songs, Sameer Anjaan blames industry monotony and exhaustion for Arijit Singh's playback singing exit: 'Every song sounds the same'
articles.summary: Noted lyricist Sameer Anjaan has weighed in on superstar singer Arijit Singh's decision to step away from playback singing, pointing to repetitiveness.
articles.body: Noted lyricist Sameer Anjaan has weighed in on superstar singer Arijit Singh's decision to step away from playback singing, pointing to repetitiveness in today's music as a key factor behind the move.Why did Sameer Anjaan say Arijit Singh left playback singing?The veteran wordsmith made these remarks during his appearance on trade analyst Komal Nahta's podcast, Game Changers: The Music Series, where the discussion centred on how excessive output can lead to creative fatigue among artists. Addressing the present scenario in playback singing, he said, "What is happening to the new artists? People gave multiple opportunities to them. We had one Arijit Singh, but he got so exhausted that he left the industry. We keep hearing the same monotonous songs, with constant repetition. Every song sounds the same."Arijit Singh officially announced his retirement from playback singing on January 27, 2026, clarifying that while he would stop taking new assignments, he would continue creating music independently.What did Sameer Anjaan say about lack of variety in music today?Continuing his thoughts, Sameer explained, "Arijit understood that if he continued doing this for longer, he would become monotonous. He wasn't getting a variety of songs; they were tailored to his singing style. All the new singers after him kept singing in the same style. In the previous generation, when we had Udit Narayan and others, there was such variety in music. Nowadays, we don't have that. That is why every sensible person in this line will eventually leave."Who is Sameer Anjaan?A Guinness World Record holder for penning the most film songs, Sameer Anjaan remains one of Bollywood's most prolific lyricists, having dominated the 1990s music scene. articles.title: Rajinikanth's ‘Dharman’ enters third schedule as Ashwath Marimuthu shares BTS video With Raashi Khanna: 'Back with Thalaivar'

articles.body: Director Ashwath Marimuthu, currently helming the much-anticipated Rajinikanth starrer Dharman, has given fans a fresh update from the sets. The filmmaker took to social media on Wednesday to confirm that the project has entered its third schedule, sharing a behind-the-scenes glimpse featuring the Superstar himself.When did Dharman's third schedule begin?Taking to his X handle, Ashwath Marimuthu posted a video showing Rajinikanth seated with his back to the camera, deep in conversation with actress Raashi Khanna on set. Captioning the clip, the director wrote:"Back with Thalaivar for 'Dharman' 3rd schedule #superstar @RKFI."The latest update arrives close on the heels of the film wrapping its second schedule, which ran from August 13 to September 4. Producer Kamal Haasan's production banner marked the milestone with its own celebratory post, writing, "Dharman 2nd Schedule Wrapped. Swag Mode: ON." A glimpse from the video showed Rajinikanth in character as a senior medical faculty member, lecturing a group of junior doctors.What is Rajinikanth's look in 'Dharman'?At the start of the second schedule, the makers had unveiled Rajinikanth's doctor avatar with the caption, "The deadly doctor. #Dharman Schedule 2 Begins, and this one's legendary. #KettaPaiyanSir."The film, earlier known by its working title 'Thalaivar173' had its first look poster shared back in June, teasing Rajinikanth's striking new avatar with the note, "We heard you !! Ithan hair styleu (This is the hair style)!! Ithan looku (This is the look)! Sexy work @kabilanchelliah." The poster depicted him inside an operation theatre, scalpel in hand, standing over a fallen rowdy — hinting at the film's dark, edgy tone.More about 'Dharman'The film boasts a solid technical lineup: music by Anirudh Ravichander, cinematography by Niketh Bommi, and editing by Pradeep E Raghav. Action sequences are choreographed by National Award-winning duo Anbariv.What's next for Rajinikanth?Ahead of 'Dharman's release, Rajinikanth will be seen in 'Jailer 2,' directed by Nelson Dilipkumar, hitting theatres on October 15, 2026.
